sat-am-1-gong.hook: We find hope and healing when we perform temple ordinances for family members with whom we may earlier have had difficult relationships.
sat-am-1-gong.text: We find hope and healing when we perform temple ordinances for family members with whom we may earlier have had difficult relationships. Jesus Christ can help us mend, forgive, move forward. We exclaim: “When I did the temple work for my family member, my heart softened.” “I could forgive.” “I was freed.” “Anger and bitterness left.” “I felt peace for the first time.” We may even come to desire sealing with those family members. Rich blessings await. Please “do not procrastinate the day of your repentance until the end.” Please do not deliberately delay the spiritual peace and joyful freedom Jesus Christ wants you to have now.
sat-am-1-gong.why: Unexpected, personal angle on temple work (healing hard family relationships) with short, quotable testimonies; exact match to print.

sat-am-1-gong.hook: Covenants are not big or small.
sat-am-1-gong.text: On occasion, some members may feel a temple is smaller or less ornate than they expected. I once heard, “Elder Gong, we are happy to have a temple but sorry it is a small temple.” I said, “Dear brother, dear sister, ordinances are not big or small. Covenants are not big or small. Please let us never speak of a temple as big or small, elaborate or plain. Let us always only speak with love and gratitude for ‘Holiness to the Lord, the House of the Lord.’”
sat-am-1-gong.why: Memorable rhetorical turn ("ordinances are not big or small"); self-contained; only "we are/it is" spoken as contractions.

sat-am-1-gong.hook: I know a family of modest means.
sat-am-1-gong.text: I know a family of modest means. At their widowed mother’s request, the children saved and purchased their mother her own ceremonial temple clothes. Their mother loved using her own temple clothing as she regularly attended the temple for many years. When their mother passed away, the family honored their mother’s request by burying her in her temple clothes. Their dear mother was ready to enter eternity prepared for the glorious Resurrection.
sat-am-1-gong.why: Tender, complete short story with a clear ending; spoken exactly as printed.

sat-am-1-gong.hook: Whatever generation you are in the Church, in the chain of your eternal family, please be a strong link.
sat-am-1-gong.text: Some new converts feel alone. But you are part of Heavenly Father’s family. And when you take family names to the temple, your eternal family extends on both sides of the veil. My father and mother joined our Church as the only members in either of their families. Today, family history and genealogy help connect many Gong and Char family generations. Whatever generation you are in the Church, in the chain of your eternal family, please be a strong link.
sat-am-1-gong.why: Direct encouragement to new converts with a vivid closing image; one printed "in" not spoken.

sat-am-1-gong.hook: So, why did the temple workers cross the road?
sat-am-1-gong.text: Dear brothers and sisters, come worship and rejoice with the Lord in the house of the Lord, in temple doctrine and in your own personal temple culture. So, why did the temple workers cross the road? So God and temple ordinances can protect, bless, and inspire; bring forgiveness, healing, and peace; and unite loved ones here and away.
sat-am-1-gong.why: Pays off the opening joke, but the joke set-up is 10 minutes earlier, so it lands softer on its own.

sat-am-1-gong.hook: We can come to the temple more often.
sat-am-1-gong.text: Today, as temples come closer in many places, we can manifest the precious spirit of temple sacrifice in new ways. We can come to the temple more often. We can search and bring more family names to bless deceased loved ones. As the seasons of our lives allow, we can regularly serve in the Lord’s house, both as temple patron and as temple ordinance worker.
sat-am-1-gong.why: Practical, but list-like; one printed "as" differs.

sat-am-2-runia.hook: And yet, without a doubt, a master’s hand had shaped what mine could not.
sat-am-2-runia.text: Let me leave this last visual image from a sculpting class my brother Kent took in college. He said: “Our final assignment was to sculpt a bust of ourselves out of clay. I thought to myself, ‘This is going to be easy enough.’ “We began, and I realized it wasn’t easy at all! When I looked at the piece, the eyes were terrible. No matter how hard I tried, I couldn’t get the eyes to look lifelike. “I observed my classmates and noticed our instructor was helping them. He was very good. “I, however, didn’t want help. I wanted this to be my piece. I struggled alone for quite a while, until I finally humbled myself and asked for help. “The instructor came over and deftly started carving; he did it so aggressively and abruptly that it startled me. He dug into the clay much further than I had, and within a few minutes the eyes came to life. It looked so good! There was no way I could have done it. “As I stepped back and looked at the piece, I could see that it was uniquely me. And yet, without a doubt, a master’s hand had shaped what mine could not.”
sat-am-2-runia.why: Vivid complete parable (the sculpting teacher) with a payoff line; exact match to print.

sat-am-2-runia.hook: But let me be clear: Not understanding is not the same as not believing.”
sat-am-2-runia.text: Still, like Nephi, I do not know the meaning of all things. When I spoke at Ryan’s funeral, I looked at his wife, Cari, and their four children with such a heavy heart and said, “I don’t understand why this happened. I don’t. But let me be clear: Not understanding is not the same as not believing.” I may not understand everything, but I absolutely believe God sees you, loves you, and knows your story—a story that is both personal and purposeful! Your story is personal. So you don’t need to look sideways and ask, “How come my life doesn’t look like theirs?” And it’s purposeful in that it has meaning. Our suffering means something. It’s not a detour from the path; it gives purpose to our path.
sat-am-2-runia.why: The talk's most quotable line, from her son's funeral; ends on "your story is personal and purposeful". Name "Cari" timing interpolated.

sat-am-2-runia.hook: The gospel isn’t the umbrella; it’s the solid rock we’re standing on during the storm
sat-am-2-runia.text: And while I know earth life is about experience, why am I so surprised every time I experience it? Maybe it’s because I grew up hearing things like “If you keep the commandments, you’ll be blessed. Pay your tithing, and the windows of heaven will open. Follow the Word of Wisdom, and you’ll have health and protection.” True promises, right? So the gospel felt like a big umbrella I could hold over my head to keep the rain from falling on me. But I’ve learned from experience that we’re all going to get rained on. And sometimes we’re going to get pelted! The gospel isn’t the umbrella; it’s the solid rock we’re standing on during the storm—that “sure foundation … whereon if men build they cannot fall.”
sat-am-2-runia.why: Fresh metaphor that reframes gospel promises; light humour then a strong turn; one contraction differs.

sat-am-2-runia.hook: You can curse God and blame Him, or you can turn to Him and let Him heal you.”
sat-am-2-runia.text: The day before Ryan died, he was set apart as the elders quorum president. That afternoon he visited a neighbor whose wife and children had just left him. When Ryan returned, he asked Cari to write down what he had told this man. Ryan said, “Brother, you have a choice right now, and it’s a big one. You can curse God and blame Him, or you can turn to Him and let Him heal you.” We all have a choice right now. Let’s choose Christ, who can heal the wounds of this world while carving out room for joy! God is saying, “Trust me,” and we are learning how to say yes.
sat-am-2-runia.why: Her late son's own words, turned into an invitation to all ("We all have a choice right now"); "Cari" and one "the" differ.

sat-am-2-runia.hook: He answered, “Yes, because you can trust the one who designed it, and it always turns out.”
sat-am-2-runia.text: At Ryan’s funeral, his oldest son, seven-year-old Jaac, shared a Primary talk he and his dad had worked on just two weeks earlier. Jaac said, “I love Lego bricks, and when I get a new box, I open it up and lay out all the pieces and follow the instructions. Just like our Heavenly Father has a plan, and if we follow, it will guide us, and we can build hard things.” Then Cari asked Jaac, “What would you do if you didn’t have the picture on the box, only the instructions? Would you still stick to the plan?” He answered, “Yes, because you can trust the one who designed it, and it always turns out.”
sat-am-2-runia.why: Sweet child's-eye lesson, but several spoken differences in the quoted dialogue.

sat-am-2-runia.text: Thirteen years ago our oldest son, Ryan, woke up on a Monday morning, kissed his wife and four young children goodbye, and left for work. A few hours later, he collapsed and died from undetected hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. His heart simply stopped. The next day was his two-year-old daughter Piper’s birthday. As we lit candles on her cake and began to sing, she was looking for her dad, and I realized this was something I would not be able to fix.
sat-am-2-runia.why: Raw and moving set-up (26 s) but no resolution on its own.

sat-am-2-runia.hook: My friends, there is sculpting taking place within each of our souls.
sat-am-2-runia.text: My friends, there is sculpting taking place within each of our souls. To invite the Savior to become involved is hard. Our pride gets in the way. He’ll lovingly chasten us to get our attention, but He waits for an invitation before He can really go to work. Then He will start carving, sometimes surprising us with how abrupt and aggressive the work feels. But as time goes on, we will begin to see the work of His hand. God is shaping us into something only He knows we can become. And one day, when all the suffering and loneliness have ended and our pain is gone, we will be able to step back and look into the mirror of our own soul. Then we will “stand all amazed” and feel to fall at the Savior’s feet and thank Him. We will thank Him for all of it—the molding, the shaping, the pain, and the adversity that have helped us become more like Him. “For we shall see him as he is,” and “we shall be like him,” I joyfully testify in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
sat-am-2-runia.why: Strong close, but 4 small spoken differences and depends on the sculpting story.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: How many “Almas” are there around you waiting to hear your witness and discover, or rediscover, the hope that is found in Jesus Christ?
sat-am-3-causse.text: At a moment of deep anguish, the young Alma remembered having “heard [his] father prophesy … concerning the coming of one Jesus Christ … to atone for the sins of the world.” That remembered witness from his father became the spark of hope that led him to repent and completely change his life. How many “Almas” are there around you waiting to hear your witness and discover, or rediscover, the hope that is found in Jesus Christ?
sat-am-3-causse.why: Scripture story to a direct, memorable question to the viewer; exact match to print.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.
sat-am-3-causse.text: One of our nieces recently shared an experience from her youth. She said: “A few years ago, when I was beginning to gain a testimony, I bore my testimony at a Young Women camp. I was so nervous that I only managed to say two simple sentences: ‘I know that God loves me’ and ‘I know that God has a plan for me.’ In the days that followed, I felt discouraged because I wished I could speak like the other girls. I talked with my mom, and she asked, ‘Do you believe what you said?’ ‘Yes,’ I replied. ‘Then that’s all that matters,’ she said.” Her mother was right. There is great power in a sincere, humble, and heartfelt testimony. It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.
sat-am-3-causse.why: Relatable story (a nervous teen's two-sentence testimony) with a quotable payoff.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: To say “I know” is a tender expression of love toward our neighbor.
sat-am-3-causse.text: To say “I know” is a tender expression of love toward our neighbor. Because we love others, we naturally desire to share with them the most precious gift we have received—our witness of Jesus Christ and His gospel. In turn, saying “I love you” with a pure and sincere heart is a way of bearing testimony of Jesus Christ. Whenever we express Christlike love to those around us, we bear witness of Him, the source of all perfect love. Brothers and sisters, I hope you will fill your lives, and the lives of others, with many heartfelt I knows—as I hope you already do with many I love yous. As these expressions of faith and love come together, they will help create an environment where the Spirit of the Lord can dwell and bring joy to your hearts.
sat-am-3-causse.why: Distinctive idea linking "I know" and "I love you"; warm invitation.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: Our testimony is not a talent to be hidden.
sat-am-3-causse.text: Like many of you, I have often wondered, “Why me? Why was I so privileged to receive a testimony of the restored gospel?” I never found a fully satisfying answer. Over time, however, I came to ask a better question: “What does the Lord expect me to do with this gift?” Our testimony is not a talent to be hidden. It is a gift to be shared—with grateful hearts and in a spirit of humility and love.
sat-am-3-causse.why: Honest "Why me?" question reframed into a better one; short; one printed "and" differs.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.
sat-am-3-causse.text: The gift of testimony is deeply personal. It is received in the intimacy of our relationship with God and shaped according to our unique experiences, circumstances, and needs. It grows through faith, earnest seeking, gospel living, and the quiet influence of the Holy Ghost. Truly, “to know that Jesus Christ is the Son of God” is one of life’s greatest blessings and a precious gift from God. Your testimony may be different from mine or that of other family members or fellow Saints. Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.
sat-am-3-causse.why: Reassuring and exact, but more abstract.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: I solemnly declare that we have a loving Heavenly Father and that His Son, Jesus Christ, is the Savior of the world and the source of “every good gift.”
sat-am-3-causse.text: As a servant of the Lord and one of His special witnesses, I am profoundly grateful for the gift of testimony I have received through the power of God. I solemnly declare that we have a loving Heavenly Father and that His Son, Jesus Christ, is the Savior of the world and the source of “every good gift.” I express my earnest desire to serve Them and to bear witness of Them continually, all the days of my life. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
sat-am-3-causse.why: Apostolic witness; formal closing, one word differs.

sat-am-3-causse.hook: I realized that my primary responsibility was simply to bear witness of the Savior.
sat-am-3-causse.text: The next morning, as I prayed for comfort and guidance, I felt prompted to open a copy of the Liahona magazine lying on our kitchen table. Almost immediately, my eyes found this reassuring promise from the Lord: “Be of good cheer, and do not fear, for I the Lord am with you, and will stand by you; and ye shall bear record of me, even Jesus Christ.” That scripture brought peace to my heart. I realized that my primary responsibility was simply to bear witness of the Savior. Everything else would be in His hands.
sat-am-3-causse.why: Personal call story, but "Liahona" and one word differ.

sat-am-4-sikahema.hook: What a blessing it is to live in a time when apostles and prophets are on the earth.
sat-am-4-sikahema.text: Perhaps you can appreciate why my beloved grandparents were so eager to be in the presence of one of the Lord’s anointed. Even in their despair and while mourning the tragic loss of their only son—their handsome, cheerful little boy—they solemnly buried him and made the Herculean effort to sail just to listen to an Apostle of the Lord. What a blessing it is to live in a time when apostles and prophets are on the earth.
sat-am-4-sikahema.why: Ties the family story to the viewer in three sentences; exact match to print.

sat-am-4-sikahema.hook: Grieving with empty arms, my grandparents got back on the boat, their mission not yet complete.
sat-am-4-sikahema.text: For the Wolfgramms, burying their infant child was akin to the pioneers who buried their children on the trail to Zion. Like the early pioneers, they yearned to hear and be in the presence of an Apostle. Grieving with empty arms, my grandparents got back on the boat, their mission not yet complete. They were sailing toward an Apostle, who held priesthood keys, held the authority for the ordinances that would later seal them as an eternal family. They sailed to sit at the feet of an Apostle, who would teach them their duty so they could bless others on their island with the message of the restored gospel of Jesus Christ.
sat-am-4-sikahema.why: Powerful image of faith after loss; the "why" of the whole talk. Family name timing interpolated.

sat-am-4-sikahema.hook: The storm left the baby severely dehydrated.
sat-am-4-sikahema.text: The Wolfgramms sailed into a storm; a journey that should have taken 16 hours to Vava‘u stretched into two and a half brutal days at sea. From my Gramma’s journal, she wrote: “We were completely soaked, … battered, and sick, … too weak to eat. … I held Vilimanulea to my chest until finally arriving to Vava‘u.” Yet their trial was not over. The storm left the baby severely dehydrated. With no medicine, the Wolfgramms’ precious son died of exposure. Within two days, they buried their baby in Vava‘u and continued their voyage.
sat-am-4-sikahema.why: Gripping first-hand journal account; names (Wolfgramm, Vilimanulea) interpolated but spoken.

sat-am-4-sikahema.hook: With that clear, simple, and understated introduction, the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, would begin the work of restoring the Savior’s ancient Church through a then-teenage boy in upstate New York.
sat-am-4-sikahema.text: With that clear, simple, and understated introduction, the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, would begin the work of restoring the Savior’s ancient Church through a then-teenage boy in upstate New York. In the years that followed this momentous event, greater truths, priesthood authority, sacred ordinances, additional scriptures, and knowledge of God’s plan of salvation would all be restored or rediscovered through the Prophet Joseph Smith.
sat-am-4-sikahema.why: Exact, but doctrinal summary without the story that gives the talk its pull.

sat-am-4-sikahema.hook: For Saints scattered across the Pacific, having an Apostle of the Lord among them was the chance of a lifetime.
sat-am-4-sikahema.text: In June of that same year, Apostle Matthew Cowley, who was over the Pacific, was coming to Tonga. Only twice before had an Apostle visited our island kingdom: David O. McKay in 1921, followed by George Albert Smith in 1938. For Saints scattered across the Pacific, having an Apostle of the Lord among them was the chance of a lifetime. Reaching the Apostle meant a long voyage for my grandparents across the largest body of water on the planet to the main island of Tongatapu, but first stopping midway on their home island of Vava‘u. The Pacific is known for its fickle weather patterns, and the week of their trip was no different.
sat-am-4-sikahema.why: Exact; sets up the voyage but has no payoff alone.

sat-am-5-hathaway.hook: Have you ever felt left out, wondered if you were enough, lost someone you loved, faced illness, experienced family difficulties, or carried a burden no one else could see?
sat-am-5-hathaway.text: Have you ever felt left out, wondered if you were enough, lost someone you loved, faced illness, experienced family difficulties, or carried a burden no one else could see? My message today is that Jesus Christ delivers the righteous from these and every other affliction of mortality. Jesus Christ descended below all things and suffered “pains and afflictions and temptations of every kind”; therefore, He comprehends our suffering, is filled with mercy, and knows how to succor us according to our infirmities. With perfect understanding and infinite power, He can deliver the righteous from all things, forever. His deliverance is certain; the question for most righteous followers is not if He will deliver but how and when He will do so.
sat-am-5-hathaway.why: A question nearly every viewer answers "yes" to, then a clear promise; exact match to print.

sat-am-5-hathaway.text: To Kenzie and all who wait for divine deliverance, I testify that the Lord is not delayed, distracted, or derelict in His deliverance. He has not forgotten you. He does not take joy in your suffering. However, He knows that lessons learned while waiting can bring converting growth that an earlier rescue might not produce.
sat-am-5-hathaway.why: Short, comforting, alliterative ("not delayed, distracted, or derelict"); exact.

sat-am-5-hathaway.hook: I have never clung so tightly to my covenants.
sat-am-5-hathaway.text: Sister Kenzie Brinkerhoff was visited in her afflictions and given sacred assurances as well. On the last preparation day before Sister Brinkerhoff returned home from her mission, her father, Kelly, called early in the morning to tell her he loved her, was proud of her, and was excited to hug her soon. Heartbreakingly, while driving home from work that night, Kelly was in a vehicle accident and passed away. When my wife and I arrived soon after Kenzie received the news, she was grieving deeply. Through her tears came the heartrending question, “President, how could this happen when I was one week away from hugging my dad?” Several weeks later I called to ask how she was dealing with her father’s passing, and she said: “The past few weeks have been the most awful and the most sacred time in my life. I have never clung so tightly to my covenants. I know that Jesus knows what this feels like, and He will heal me.”
sat-am-5-hathaway.why: Heartbreaking true story with a faith-filled answer; "Sister Brinkerhoff returned" timing interpolated; 71 s.

sat-am-5-hathaway.hook: In that moment, the Spirit brought us peace: Everything would be all right.
sat-am-5-hathaway.text: Our family experienced a sudden trial and the Lord’s deliverance as we drove in two cars to begin our service as mission leaders. While driving in a construction zone, two large tires came loose from a semitruck and struck both cars at high speed. The airbags deployed, the cars were destroyed, and we were left stranded on the roadside wondering why this had happened when we had left everything to serve the Lord. In that moment, the Spirit brought us peace: Everything would be all right. We were not immediately delivered from the trial, but that assurance gave us hope in the deliverance that would come. With the help of many wonderful people, we arrived on time and began our mission without serious injury.
sat-am-5-hathaway.why: Dramatic personal story (tires hit both cars) with a clear spiritual lesson; one "and" differs.

sat-am-5-hathaway.hook: But Jesus said, “Be not afraid, only believe.”
sat-am-5-hathaway.text: But what of moments when the hour seems too late, the loss too final, and deliverance appears impossible? Surely, Jairus must have felt the time had passed and deliverance was impossible when he received news that his daughter had died. But Jesus said, “Be not afraid, only believe.” Holding on to that assurance, Jairus watched the Savior deliver his daughter from death, showing that no mortal timeline can place us beyond Christ’s power to deliver.
sat-am-5-hathaway.why: Exact, scripture story, slightly less personal.

sat-am-5-hathaway.hook: Some miracles are immediate, some come after long waiting, and some await the Resurrection.
sat-am-5-hathaway.text: When deliverance feels impossible, remember Elder Patrick Kearon’s witness: “Jesus specializes in the seemingly impossible. He came here to make the impossible possible, the irredeemable redeemable, to heal the unhealable, to right the unrightable, to promise the unpromisable. And He’s really good at it. In fact, He’s perfect at it.” To all who continue to face the pain, fear, and loneliness of life, I echo the Savior’s words: “Be not afraid, only believe.” In His time and way, Jesus Christ will deliver you. Some miracles are immediate, some come after long waiting, and some await the Resurrection.
sat-am-5-hathaway.why: Great Kearon quote, but "Kearon’s" and "right unrightable" timings differ.

sat-am-6-soares.hook: Through the union of fasting and prayer, our faith, love, and devotion to Him deepen.
sat-am-6-soares.text: A sincere and faithful fast is accompanied by earnest and intentional prayer. As we lift our hearts to the Lord in humility, fasting becomes an expression of our desire to draw near to Him, communicate the true desires of our hearts, and understand His will for us. Through the union of fasting and prayer, our faith, love, and devotion to Him deepen. We become more humble and more aware of our complete dependence upon the Lord. Our hearts are softened, our souls become more receptive to the influence of the Holy Ghost, and we are better prepared to receive personal revelation and move forward along the covenant path.
sat-am-6-soares.why: Clear, practical heart of the talk; exact match to print.

sat-am-6-soares.hook: I have personally witnessed how the blessings of fasting often enter people’s lives quietly and tenderly—softening hearts, strengthening testimonies, sanctifying souls, and transforming lives.
sat-am-6-soares.text: I have personally witnessed how the blessings of fasting often enter people’s lives quietly and tenderly—softening hearts, strengthening testimonies, sanctifying souls, and transforming lives. I have also seen sacred blessings come to those who turn their hearts toward God’s children through generous fast offerings. Personally, I have felt an increase of inspiration and revelation as I have sought to live this law with greater sincerity. Fasting, when observed with joy and joined with prayer and generosity, brings sweeter communion with the Lord and a deeper, more personal connection with Him.
sat-am-6-soares.why: Personal apostolic witness of what fasting does; exact.

sat-am-6-soares.hook: As in all things, the Savior did not merely teach divine principles—He exemplified them perfectly.
sat-am-6-soares.text: This divine pattern finds its highest and holiest expression in the life of Jesus Christ. As in all things, the Savior did not merely teach divine principles—He exemplified them perfectly. Before His earthly ministry began, He withdrew into the wilderness and spent 40 days communing with His Father. He was the Only Begotten Son of God in the flesh, and of all the things He could have done to prepare for His sacred mission, He chose to seek complete alignment with His Father’s will through earnest fasting and prayer.
sat-am-6-soares.why: Christ's 40-day fast as the model; exact.

sat-am-6-soares.hook: Though our fast offerings may seem small and simple, they become consecrated expressions of compassion, concern, and service.
sat-am-6-soares.text: Though our fast offerings may seem small and simple, they become consecrated expressions of compassion, concern, and service. As we give generously—not only for the benefit of those in need but also as an expression of our love for the Lord and our commitment to His work—we consecrate both our means and our time to Him. In doing so, we give more fully of ourselves to the building of the kingdom of God.

sat-am-6-soares.hook: As you do so, I promise, in the name of our Savior, Jesus Christ, that miracles will come into your life.
sat-am-6-soares.text: My dear friends, I invite you to prayerfully ponder Isaiah’s teachings and more intentionally embrace the divine purpose of the law of the fast in a higher and holier way as part of our worship. As you do so, I promise, in the name of our Savior, Jesus Christ, that miracles will come into your life. You will draw nearer to the Savior, receive strength to overcome your weaknesses, and become more sensitive to the needs of others. Through this divinely appointed practice, the Lord will sanctify us and pour His Spirit and blessings more abundantly into our lives.
sat-am-6-soares.why: Apostolic promise, but two printed words differ.

sat-am-6-soares.hook: It is a way to align our desires with His purposes, and our expectations with His wisdom.
sat-am-6-soares.text: Adopting this holy pattern of fasting is more than a physical test of restraint or a petition for specific blessings. It is an elevating expression of faith and trust in the Lord through which our hearts can be filled with rejoicing as we commune with Him more deeply. It is a way to align our desires with His purposes, and our expectations with His wisdom. Even when answers do not come in the way we expect, fasting and prayer help us develop greater confidence in the Lord, in our covenants with Him, and in His plan for our lives, as well as a deeper willingness to accept His will.
sat-am-6-soares.why: Good line, but two words differ and it is abstract.

sat-am-7-douglas.text: We love missionaries of all ages. You are an army of righteousness with the doctrine of Christ as your purpose. You are a force of faith, power, love, and joy. You are what you preach. You are not only the messengers but also living examples of the message. Make no mistake—you are doing the most important work you could be doing. We thank you for building up the kingdom of God on earth.
sat-am-7-douglas.why: Punchy, energetic direct address to missionaries; two tiny word differences.

sat-am-7-douglas.hook: “I only want to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him.”
sat-am-7-douglas.text: Sister Douglas and I served as mission leaders in Lima, Peru. One of our amazing missionaries was Elder Merlin Sanchez. Merlin was baptized when he was nearly 24 years old. As some do, he stopped participating for a time. A faithful friend helped him begin to fill out his mission papers and schedule a physical exam, even though Merlin had not yet decided to serve a mission. With the help of friends and leaders, Merlin returned to church at age 25. A desire to serve a mission suddenly swelled in his heart. Thankfully, his mission papers were well advanced. Once he made the decision to go, it was miraculous to see how the Lord removed seemingly insurmountable obstacles one by one. When I asked him why he wanted to serve, he replied, “I only want to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him.”
sat-am-7-douglas.why: Complete convert story (back to church at 25, then a mission) with a simple, moving answer.

sat-am-7-douglas.hook: There is still plenty of room and a special place reserved for each one of you!
sat-am-7-douglas.text: We rejoice exceedingly for your faithful response to the prophet’s call to action. Record numbers of missionaries of all ages are finding great joy as they humbly dedicate themselves to serving the Lord by laboring among Heavenly Father’s children. I wish to wholeheartedly add: There is still plenty of room and a special place reserved for each one of you! We need you! “Come join the ranks!” You have a testimony of Jesus Christ and His Atonement that can bless a world suffering without knowledge of His divine mission. I pray that you will make the Savior’s grand commission your very own.
sat-am-7-douglas.why: Upbeat invitation ("We need you! Come join the ranks!"); one "the" differs.

sat-am-7-douglas.hook: We could say this is in your spiritual DNA.
sat-am-7-douglas.text: Yes, the Lord’s expectations are high for you! But, oh, is it worth it! President Russell M. Nelson taught, “Nothing else compares in magnitude, nothing else compares in importance, nothing else compares in majesty.” God held you in reserve for this time. You were taught and prepared, before you were born, to invite God’s children to come unto Christ. We could say this is in your spiritual DNA. Take care not to become distracted. Prioritize it; don’t let anything get in the way. You are needed!
sat-am-7-douglas.why: Fun line, but the Nelson quote and "this time" have timing differences.

sat-am-7-douglas.hook: Don’t be distracted by alternatives of far less worth.
sat-am-7-douglas.text: To you wonderful young converts of the Church, a mission may not have been on your radar, but it ought to be now. To all the rising generation of the Church, I invite you to place serving a full-time mission high on your list. Don’t be distracted by alternatives of far less worth. Some might be like Amulek of the Book of Mormon, who expressed, “For I was called many times and I would not hear.”
sat-am-7-douglas.why: Direct invitation; one word differs; 27 s.

sat-am-8-christofferson.hook: For us as Latter-day Saints, overarching all other concerns is the fact that gambling is morally wrong.
sat-am-8-christofferson.text: For us as Latter-day Saints, overarching all other concerns is the fact that gambling is morally wrong. Gambling is built on the desire to obtain something for nothing. Its structure requires that any gain comes at others’ expense. It’s hard to reconcile that with the commandment to love our neighbor as ourselves. In addition, our resources are stewardships, and the question is not merely whether a purchase is legal but whether it builds anything—in us, in our families, or in those around us. In the end, gambling produces nothing of value and enriches only its purveyors.
sat-am-8-christofferson.why: The clearest statement of the talk; tight reasoning in 40 s; one phrase timing differs.

sat-am-8-christofferson.hook: Perhaps you think your character and your commitment to divine covenants are sufficiently strong that, for you, wagers would never become more than occasional, casual fun.
sat-am-8-christofferson.text: Perhaps you think your character and your commitment to divine covenants are sufficiently strong that, for you, wagers would never become more than occasional, casual fun. Maybe. But whether you are right about that or not, have you considered how your example might affect others? If your moral standing is secure, then undoubtedly there are others who look to you as a guide for upright living. That would certainly be true for your children but also others that you may or may not know who are watching and learning from what they see in you. They may be newer or weaker in the faith. A little gambling that seemingly has only a minor impact in your life may be more costly to them if they take license from your example.
sat-am-8-christofferson.why: Anticipates the viewer's objection ("Maybe.") then turns it to influence on others.

sat-am-8-christofferson.hook: Surveys reveal that people know that in gambling the odds are stacked against them, and the house always wins—they just don’t think it will win against them personally.
sat-am-8-christofferson.text: Surveys reveal that people know that in gambling the odds are stacked against them, and the house always wins—they just don’t think it will win against them personally. But the central risk of gambling is not merely that customers lose money on individual wagers. The larger concern is that continuous, mobile access can transform occasional entertainment into repeated behavior that displaces saving, increases debt, and creates far-reaching family and social costs. I have to agree with George Washington when he said of gambling, “It is the child of avarice—the brother of inequity—and father of mischief” (although calling it “mischief” may be too mild).
sat-am-8-christofferson.why: Sharp insight plus a witty Washington quote; exact.

sat-am-8-christofferson.hook: Today, I am pleading with all of us to live life on a higher plane.
sat-am-8-christofferson.text: Today, I am pleading with all of us to live life on a higher plane. God has granted life and agency to each of us, and each of us is accountable to Him for how we live that life. A key part of a life well-lived is contributing to the well-being of others. It is being productive in worthy endeavors. It is being and doing better without others doing worse. It comes by supporting and rewarding work rather than idle pursuits. Work leads to prosperous, just, and equitable societies. Gambling, even for fun, leads in the opposite direction.
sat-am-8-christofferson.why: Positive vision of a life well-lived; "It is" spoken as contractions.

sat-am-8-christofferson.hook: The smartphone has transformed gambling from an occasional activity requiring a trip to a casino, racetrack, or lottery kiosk into an activity available continuously, privately, and almost anywhere.
sat-am-8-christofferson.text: Putting money or something of value at risk to bet on a particular outcome or event is an activity that has plagued mankind almost, I suppose, from the beginning of time. And time has not made it any more worthwhile or any less harmful. Unfortunately, in recent years, gambling has become incredibly pervasive. The smartphone has transformed gambling from an occasional activity requiring a trip to a casino, racetrack, or lottery kiosk into an activity available continuously, privately, and almost anywhere. This has led to an explosion in gambling.

sat-am-8-christofferson.hook: What is the opportunity cost of gambling?
sat-am-8-christofferson.text: At different times, President Dallin H. Oaks has reminded us that “as we make current decisions, we should always be asking, ‘Where will this lead?’ … What is the effect on our future of the decisions we make in the present?” President Oaks points out that each choice has an “opportunity cost,” that is, “if we spend time doing one thing, we lose the opportunity to do another.” What is the opportunity cost of gambling? What do you forgo in terms of money, time, relationships, and worthwhile pursuits? Where does it lead?

sat-pm-1-renlund.hook: Neither are you, brothers and sisters; there is no asterisk excluding you from God’s richest blessings.
sat-pm-1-renlund.text: I remember learning a lesson, one of many, from my younger sister, Linda. She said that she would read her scriptures and see remarkable blessings promised by the Lord. In her mind, though, she saw a big asterisk that seemed to say, “Those blessings apply to everyone—except Linda.” Over the years, Linda came to a different realization. She said, “I am not extraordinary enough to warrant an exception. The blessings are promised to me too.” Linda is extraordinary but still no exception. Neither are you, brothers and sisters; there is no asterisk excluding you from God’s richest blessings. If you think there is, take out a big eraser and obliterate that asterisk. You can rely on God’s promises.
sat-pm-1-renlund.why: Memorable image (erase the asterisk) that speaks to anyone who feels excluded; tiny contraction differences.

sat-pm-1-renlund.hook: Through clenched teeth, Mr. Martin replied, “The oatmeal isn’t hot, and the milk isn’t cold!”
sat-pm-1-renlund.text: He was sitting on his bed, gripping his breakfast tray, and was clearly irritated. I asked what was wrong. Through clenched teeth, Mr. Martin replied, “The oatmeal isn’t hot, and the milk isn’t cold!” For the past three weeks, Mr. Martin had hovered near death yet was now complaining about the hospital food! (I think when you go through something like Mr. Martin did, you use up all your coping coupons. And I don’t think anybody should be tortured with oatmeal regardless of temperature.) But at that moment, Mr. Martin focused on the cold oatmeal in front of him and seemingly dismissed the miracle he had experienced. He lost sight of the bigger picture, both where he had been and the promise the future now held.
sat-pm-1-renlund.why: Funny, true heart-transplant story with a clear lesson; humour lands on its own.

sat-pm-1-renlund.hook: Perhaps you have been served more than your share of cold oatmeal.
sat-pm-1-renlund.text: Perhaps you have been served more than your share of cold oatmeal. Perhaps, like the children of Israel, you have doubted God’s care for you, His willingness to succor you, or His capacity to keep His promises. Yet God invites us to trust Him and His promises. During His mortal ministry, the Savior told His disciples: “These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.” Jesus overcame the world; we do not have to do so ourselves. When our faith is centered on Jesus Christ, He promises spiritual peace no matter our circumstances. We can experience joy in our here and now because of Him and through our covenant relationship with Him.
sat-pm-1-renlund.why: Applies the metaphor to the viewer and points to Christ; several "you have/do not" spoken as contractions.

sat-pm-1-renlund.text: With Moroni, I declare, “The eternal purposes of the Lord shall roll on, until all his promises shall be fulfilled.” We can trust the Lord, especially His promises. These promises apply to you. We can joyfully sing: Standing on the promises of Christ, my King, … Standing on the promises that cannot fail … Standing on the promises, I cannot fall, … Standing on the promises of God.
sat-pm-1-renlund.why: Short, warm, ends with the hymn lines; exact.

sat-pm-1-renlund.hook: Yet his righteousness would not be the source of his redemption.
sat-pm-1-renlund.text: Faith in Jesus Christ frees us from uncertainty because our hope rests on His faithfulness and righteousness, not on our own. The prophet Lehi testified to his son Jacob, “Wherefore, I know that thou art redeemed, because of the righteousness of thy Redeemer.” Jacob was a good and faithful person. Yet his righteousness would not be the source of his redemption. No, Jacob’s redemption would come through the righteousness of Jesus Christ. The same is true for each of us.

sat-pm-1-renlund.hook: They survived because of God’s miracles, yet they repeatedly focused on cold oatmeal.
sat-pm-1-renlund.text: This is not just a modern phenomenon. As recorded in the Old Testament, the Lord led the children of Israel out of slavery in Egypt. God saved them when they were trapped at the Red Sea and provided for them when they lacked food and water. Even when they complained about a monotonous diet, the Lord miraculously helped them. They survived because of God’s miracles, yet they repeatedly focused on cold oatmeal. As they overlooked both the Lord’s blessings and His promises, their trust eroded in God and in God’s prophet, Moses.
sat-pm-1-renlund.why: Clever but depends on the oatmeal story.

sat-pm-2-farnes.hook: He said, “Brother, tell me how you are really doing.”
sat-pm-2-farnes.text: So I went to the temple, but not with the best attitude. As I entered the dressing room, grumbling to myself, I heard someone say, “How are you, brother?” It was Elder Dallin H. Oaks. We had never met before, and I wasn’t about to tell a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles how discouraged I felt. So I forced a smile and said, “Everything’s great!” I changed into my temple clothes, and as I walked out, to my surprise, Elder Oaks was waiting for me. He said, “Brother, tell me how you are really doing.” Something about the compassion in his voice helped me open up. Elder Oaks listened. He expressed sincere gratitude, said some encouraging words, and even answered my administrative question. Then he gave me a big hug, and in an instant I went from feeling like giving up to feeling like I could give my whole soul in service to the Lord.
sat-pm-2-farnes.why: Discouraged bishop meets Elder Oaks in the temple dressing room; a hug changes everything. Site timings interpolate a few words, but the caption track agrees.

sat-pm-2-farnes.hook: To Jesus, these people were not interrupting His mission. They were His mission.
sat-pm-2-farnes.text: When Jesus was asked, “What shall I do to inherit eternal life?” He answered with a story about a man who had eyes to see. In the story, a traveler lay wounded on the road to Jericho. Where others saw an inconvenience or an interruption, one man saw an opportunity to minister—a divine appointment. Seeing awakened compassion. Compassion moved him to act. And his actions changed a life forever. This pattern defined the Savior’s ministry. He turned ordinary encounters with people into extraordinary moments of healing, encouragement, and transformation. To Jesus, these people were not interrupting His mission. They were His mission. God has given us eyes to see. When we use them, we begin to recognize divine appointments all around us. What once looked like random encounters become invitations from the Lord to minister with compassion. That’s what the Savior did. It’s what His prophet does.
sat-pm-2-farnes.why: The Good Samaritan as a "divine appointment"; quotable core of the talk.

sat-pm-2-farnes.hook: Brothers and sisters, let us pray every day for eyes to see the divine appointments God places before us!
sat-pm-2-farnes.text: What we did for that elder didn’t require much of us, but this ordinary encounter became a divine appointment we will always treasure. All we had to do was see the person God had placed in our path, look with compassion rather than judgment, and then act. Brothers and sisters, let us pray every day for eyes to see the divine appointments God places before us! Let us put compassion into action and minister to the person in front of us. It’s what Jesus did. And it’s what we do.

Five years later, my wife and I were invited to meet with Elder Oaks in his office. You can imagine my excitement to reminisce about the experience we had shared. I asked him, “Do you remember the conversation we had in the temple?” “I don’t think so,” he said. “Have we met before?” I recounted the experience and reminded him how his act of compassion had lifted my spirits and changed my life. Elder Oaks responded, “I’m sorry, brother. I don’t remember that.”
sat-pm-2-farnes.why: Funny, humbling payoff to the temple story; exact.

sat-pm-2-farnes.hook: It means that when someone encounters us, they should experience something of Jesus Christ—His kindness, His patience, His hope, His love, His compassion.
sat-pm-2-farnes.text: That means we choose to see as He sees, feel as He feels, and do as He would do. His life should be reflected in ours. It means that when someone encounters us, they should experience something of Jesus Christ—His kindness, His patience, His hope, His love, His compassion. Our promise of willingness is met by the Lord’s promise that we can always have His Spirit with us. With that gift, we can minister as the Savior would, with His power and His loving kindness. We make the covenant during sacred time with God every Sunday. A way we keep the covenant is by ministering to God’s children every day. Often this happens when God places someone in our path and we have eyes to see them. I call these “divine appointments.”
sat-pm-2-farnes.why: Good doctrine; a couple of words timing-interpolated.

sat-pm-3-chigbundu.hook: He said, “I am happy now and do not want to be sent home any longer.”
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.text: While serving as mission leader, I received a new missionary. In our welcome interview, this young missionary began to cry and asked to be sent home. When I asked why, he couldn’t find the right words to explain. Then I asked him if he had a testimony of the Book of Mormon. He said, “President, I don’t.” I bore my testimony of the Book of Mormon and then encouraged him to begin to study the scriptures, especially the Book of Mormon. He and his trainer made a scripture study plan. Later I received a letter from this missionary testifying of how daily scripture study had helped him understand his purpose as a missionary. He said, “I am happy now and do not want to be sent home any longer.”
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.why: Complete, honest story (a homesick missionary without a testimony) resolved through scripture study.

sat-pm-3-chigbundu.hook: I see His hands all around me, telling me, ‘My daughter, all is well.’”
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.text: While serving as an Area Seventy, I attended a stake conference in Côte d’Ivoire. After the Saturday adult session, the stake president and I decided to visit a sister who is battling with cancer. When we asked how she was feeling, she said something that remains with me to this day: “As I pray daily, I realize that the Savior loves me. I see His hands all around me, telling me, ‘My daughter, all is well.’” As we pray in faith, our spiritual immunity will be strengthened.
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.why: A sister battling cancer testifies of prayer; short, tender, ends on the talk's theme.

sat-pm-3-chigbundu.hook: During this period I reflected not on my physical immunity but on what I call “spiritual immunity.”
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.text: I learned that immunity is the body’s inherent biological ability to defend and protect itself against infectious diseases, harmful substances, and foreign invaders. During this period I reflected not on my physical immunity but on what I call “spiritual immunity.” I pray for the help of the Holy Ghost as we consider some of the ways to build our spiritual immunity. We live in troubled times marked by wars, family challenges, and economic uncertainty. Yet, as frightening as these challenges may be, we need not fear! As we build our spiritual immunity, we develop the strength and courage to withstand the challenges of life.
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.why: Introduces the fresh, memorable "spiritual immunity" idea with hope ("we need not fear!").

sat-pm-3-chigbundu.hook: questions will be replaced by “What can I learn, and what can I change?”
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.text: As we partake of the sacrament, we can ask ourselves, “What would He have me do?” As we remember Jesus Christ throughout the week and strive to keep His commandments, our lives are gradually refined and reshaped. Our “Why me?” questions will be replaced by “What can I learn, and what can I change?”
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.why: Nice reframe, but short (25 s) and a few word timings interpolated.

sat-pm-3-chigbundu.hook: While they may seem small and simple, they are truly the armor of God that will help us stand against the tactics of the devil!
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.text: My beloved brothers and sisters, I invite you to always remember scriptures, prayers, the sacrament, and covenants. While they may seem small and simple, they are truly the armor of God that will help us stand against the tactics of the devil!
sat-pm-3-chigbundu.why: Good summary line; 21 s; two word timings interpolated.

sat-pm-4-giuffra.hook: There are no exceptions to this commandment.”
sat-pm-4-giuffra.text: President Caballero read to me the account of the widow’s mite and then said, “Elder Giuffra, you are no one to deny this sister the blessings of the law of tithing. There are no exceptions to this commandment.” Those words became engraved upon my heart. My companion and I decided to pray and fast because two days later we would return to review the commandments once again before her baptism. When we arrived at her home and began reviewing the lessons, we came once again to the law of tithing. She said to us, “Last night I knelt in prayer and told Heavenly Father that I truly wanted to become a member of His Church and that He would need to help me live this law.” As we heard those words, a profound feeling of peace and assurance filled our minds and hearts. We knew that the Lord had heard both her prayers and ours. She was baptized the following Saturday.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.why: Turning point of a moving tithing story: a poor widow's faith and prayer; ends with her baptism.

sat-pm-4-giuffra.hook: We keep the commandments because we love God, not merely because we hope to receive the blessings that come from obedience.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.text: My wife often teaches a principle that has become very meaningful in our family: We keep the commandments because we love God, not merely because we hope to receive the blessings that come from obedience. Commandments are given to draw us closer to the Savior, to protect us, and to help us remain free from sin and many of the challenges the world presents. This does not mean that we will be free from trials or difficulties. All of us will face moments of uncertainty, financial hardship, illness, or loss. Yet even when we do not understand the purpose of our trials, we can have the assurance that the Lord knows our circumstances, honors our obedience, and fulfills His promises in His own time and way.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.why: A quotable family principle plus honest realism about trials.

sat-pm-4-giuffra.hook: I don’t think I will ever be able to live the law of tithing because I will not have enough money to do so.”
sat-pm-4-giuffra.text: When we began teaching the law of tithing and the promised blessings that come to those who obey it, with great sadness she said to me, “Elder Giuffra, I clean houses and wash clothes for several families. What I earn is barely enough to pay the rent for the room where we live, buy a small amount of firewood to keep us warm, and provide some food. I don’t think I will ever be able to live the law of tithing because I will not have enough money to do so.” We were deeply moved. Everything she said made sense from a worldly perspective. Although we bore testimony of the great blessings the Lord promises to those who obey this commandment, she insisted that she could not do it.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.why: Relatable objection voiced by a 70-year-old investigator; sets up the faith lesson.

sat-pm-4-giuffra.hook: I have known children of God who once could not afford a pair of shoes and who today, through faith and diligent effort, own successful businesses.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.text: During my years of service in Central America, I have seen men and women prosper both temporally and spiritually. I have met families who once worried about their next meal but who now enjoy greater stability. I have known children of God who once could not afford a pair of shoes and who today, through faith and diligent effort, own successful businesses. I have also witnessed the Lord open doors for employment, provide education, strengthen marriages, and fill faithful hearts with peace and hope.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.why: Concrete eyewitness evidence of blessings; 36 s.

sat-pm-4-giuffra.hook: I testify that the law of tithing is a law of faith.
sat-pm-4-giuffra.text: I testify that the law of tithing is a law of faith. As we obey it, we demonstrate our trust in the Lord and allow Him to work miracles in our lives, often in ways we do not expect. Christ lives. This is His Church, and President Dallin H. Oaks is His prophet.

sat-pm-5-morgan.hook: No time or effort is ever wasted in reading the Book of Mormon.
sat-pm-5-morgan.text: There are only two things I remember from that reading of the Book of Mormon by my mother: “and it came to pass” and “wars and rumors of wars.” That’s it. But more than any words that I heard or did not hear, I knew the Book of Mormon was important to my mother. And I knew she knew it was true. Even as a single mother, she made the extraordinary effort to read the Book of Mormon to me every day until it was finished. As she did, she was fulfilling the admonition of the Lord, who said, “Remember the new covenant, even the Book of Mormon.” The lesson I learned is this: No time or effort is ever wasted in reading the Book of Mormon. Not for you, not for your children, not for your family, not for anyone.
sat-pm-5-morgan.why: Funny and touching ("and it came to pass" was all he remembered) with a universal lesson; nearly exact.

sat-pm-5-morgan.hook: If you are wondering whether you or a loved one has wandered so far away that the love of God and His covenantal power cannot reach you—I say to you, you have not.
sat-pm-5-morgan.text: If you are wondering whether you or a loved one has wandered so far away that the love of God and His covenantal power cannot reach you—I say to you, you have not. As President Jeffrey R. Holland so beautifully said: “You have not traveled beyond the reach of divine love. It is not possible for you to sink lower than the infinite light of Christ’s Atonement shines.” The Atonement of Jesus Christ is the fulfillment of the greatest promise God made—that Jesus Christ would be our Savior and Redeemer. The power and reach of that covenant is infinite and eternal.
sat-pm-5-morgan.why: Direct, hopeful promise to parents of wandering children; includes Holland's famous line.

sat-pm-5-morgan.hook: Your story, your family’s story, is not all written.
sat-pm-5-morgan.text: Some may be crying out right now, with words like “O, God, where art Thou? My child is struggling.” Take comfort; God hears you and will answer your prayers in His own time and in His own way. Keep your covenants, strive to be faithful, and “cheerfully do all things that lie in [your] power; and then may [you] stand still, with the utmost assurance, to see the salvation of God, and for his arm to be revealed.” I testify that the infinite power of God is in our covenants. Don’t ever give up. Your story, your family’s story, is not all written. God is the author and the finisher of it. I am a standing, breathing, believing demonstration of God’s love and the power of God in covenants.
sat-pm-5-morgan.why: Comfort to struggling parents ending in a personal witness ("a standing, breathing, believing demonstration"); exact.

sat-pm-5-morgan.hook: It was covenants; I felt it in that moment.
sat-pm-5-morgan.text: I was retelling this experience and pondering how a young boy such as me would have an interest in religion. There were many good influences in my life, to be sure, but that did not seem to explain it all. While I was musing out loud about this topic, my wife, Rebecca, said, “I know what it was! It was covenants.” You see, while my ancestors were united with the Saints in Nauvoo, they had made covenants in the temple. Rebecca then read some of the beautiful and comforting prophetic teachings on this topic, which provide that because of “the eternal sealings of faithful parents and the divine promises made to them[,] … though some of the sheep may wander, the eye of the Shepherd is upon them, and sooner or later they will feel the tentacles of Divine Providence reaching out after them and drawing them back to the fold.” It was covenants; I felt it in that moment. And in these words, we begin to feel a sense of the awesome power of God in our covenants.
sat-pm-5-morgan.why: His wife's insight ("It was covenants") about ancestors' temple covenants; two small timing differences; 63 s.

sat-pm-5-morgan.hook: So, for two months I attended both my family’s congregation, and secretly—hiding between the accordion doors of the overflow—I attended a congregation of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
sat-pm-5-morgan.text: Because of my mother’s extraordinary efforts, I knew the Book of Mormon was true and that Joseph Smith was a prophet of God. Even so, I was confused and uncertain as to where the true Church of Jesus Christ was. When I was 14, I began to question the church of my childhood. I knew members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints; they were my friends. All of this led me to sincerely seek the truth. So, for two months I attended both my family’s congregation, and secretly—hiding between the accordion doors of the overflow—I attended a congregation of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. I can’t fully express the gratitude I have for my upbringing and the knowledge I had received; even so, I came to know that this is the Lord’s Church.
sat-pm-5-morgan.why: Vivid conversion detail; exact; depends on context.

sat-pm-5-morgan.hook: Like the great binding power of gravity that stretches across the universe, covenants with God stretch over all time and all space.
sat-pm-5-morgan.text: Covenants with God are filled with incalculable power. They do not bless just the maker of the covenant but are generational in their impact. We are all the intended beneficiaries of countless covenants! Like the great binding power of gravity that stretches across the universe, covenants with God stretch over all time and all space.

sat-pm-6-fale.hook: You did not earn it; you cannot lose it.
sat-pm-6-fale.text: While at a Church meeting last year, I received an impression to do what the teacher was doing. So, in a text, I asked my wife to find a baby picture of each of our children. When I got home, we sat down and showed my kids their pictures. I told them that there are no words to fully express the love we felt when they were born, including the day each picture was taken. I then asked, “As of the date of this picture, what had you done to earn our love?” They lowered their eyes and said, “Nothing.” I asked them to look up and said, “You are right. You did nothing to earn our love. By that same token, there is nothing you can ever do that will unearn or remove that love from you. You did not earn it; you cannot lose it. It is yours forever.”
sat-pm-6-fale.why: Perfect short-form story: baby pictures, "what had you done to earn our love?", "Nothing." Exact.

sat-pm-6-fale.hook: no matter what has happened, you can always come home, just as you can always turn to your Father in Heaven.”
sat-pm-6-fale.text: I continued, “We need you to always remember that what we feel is but a small fraction of what your Heavenly Father feels for you. You are His child and He loves you. He loved you before you were born, He loves you today, and He will love you tomorrow. He wants you to prepare to be like Him. You must never forget this. We hope this understanding gives you courage to do your best, to trust Him, and to live up to your potential. We also hope it gives you the strength and the humility to come home when you need to, because no matter what has happened, you can always come home, just as you can always turn to your Father in Heaven.” There were tears and tender hearts as the Holy Spirit bore witness that this was true.
sat-pm-6-fale.why: Continues the story into God's love and "you can always come home"; one word differs.

sat-pm-6-fale.hook: We become quick to repent, slow to judge, and ever hopeful that the best is yet before us.
sat-pm-6-fale.text: Second, when we understand God’s love for us and for the rest of His children, we become immune to the divisive and misleading labels of our fallen world, both the labels that people try to put on us and the labels the world tries to put on others. We see ourselves and all of God’s children as beloved and divine. We become quick to repent, slow to judge, and ever hopeful that the best is yet before us. We are forever willing to love and to make sure that no one is ever sitting, standing, or walking alone.
sat-pm-6-fale.why: Timely point about labels and belonging; one "and" differs.

sat-pm-6-fale.hook: Third, understanding our Father’s love protects us from the pernicious lie that it is too late for someone to change, too late for someone to turn to Christ, and too late to receive His redeeming grace.
sat-pm-6-fale.text: Third, understanding our Father’s love protects us from the pernicious lie that it is too late for someone to change, too late for someone to turn to Christ, and too late to receive His redeeming grace. From the prodigal son to leaving the 99 sheep to find the one, our Father’s message, through His Son, has always been that there is still yet time if we turn to Christ today. God’s love is real, and Jesus Christ is evidence of that love.
sat-pm-6-fale.why: Hope for anyone who feels it's too late; "99" spoken as words.

sat-pm-7-kearon.hook: What does living in lift actually look like?
sat-pm-7-kearon.text: What does living in lift actually look like? A few simple things. Find a faithful guide and learn from them where lift is found. Actively tune in to the sweet feelings of the Holy Spirit and the things in your life that lead you there. Join those who are climbing. Do what they do. Watch closely for the subtle signs of sink in your own life, and turn away decisively. And when you find lift yourself, show someone else where and how to rise! Then soar in the joy of the Lord!
sat-pm-7-kearon.why: Practical, rhythmic list ("Join those who are climbing. Do what they do."); exact.

sat-pm-7-kearon.hook: In gliding, if you are not actively climbing in lift, you are descending.
sat-pm-7-kearon.text: In gliding, if you are not actively climbing in lift, you are descending. This is an uncomfortable fact. A descent can be so gradual that, unless you watch your altitude, you may not notice you are sinking. Isn’t it the same in our lives? How easy it is to slowly slip from spiritual heights we have worked so hard to climb when we neglect the practices and behaviours that brought us there. We rarely intend to sink. We want lift—its joy and blessings—but we may not recognise the quiet cost of neglecting vital communion with our Father, Saviour, and the Holy Spirit.
sat-pm-7-kearon.why: Sharp, memorable spiritual analogy ("We rarely intend to sink.").

sat-pm-7-kearon.hook: At the heart of our faith is the glorious truth that we have an adoring Father in Heaven, whose Son, our Saviour, loves to lift!
sat-pm-7-kearon.text: At the heart of our faith is the glorious truth that we have an adoring Father in Heaven, whose Son, our Saviour, loves to lift! Just think of all the scriptural accounts that show our Redeemer lifting people from despair, out of their figurative “sink.” With His all-powerful hand, He lifted His beloved Peter from sinking in the waves; He lifted the daughter of Jairus from the depths of death; and after healing the boy plagued with an unclean spirit who “was as one dead; … Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up.” Our Saviour constantly sought out the most desperate souls sinking into darkness and dread and lifted them up. And He wants to lift you!
sat-pm-7-kearon.why: The talk's title truth with scripture images; ends "And He wants to lift you!" ("Saviour" British spelling = spoken word).

sat-pm-7-kearon.hook: You cannot see it, but you can see what it does.
sat-pm-7-kearon.text: The crucial skill in gliding is finding rising air. You cannot see it, but you can see what it does. I was taught to look for cumulus clouds because they often mark where warm air is rising, and I learned to fly toward them. But even more important than using visual cues to find rising air is to learn to feel it. While flying along, I would begin to feel that I was being lifted by an unseen force. This rising air is called “lift.” One wing would tip upward, and I would turn toward it, into the lift.
sat-pm-7-kearon.why: Vivid aviation set-up; one word differs.

sat-pm-7-kearon.text: Remember: our Father sent His magnificent Son to be lifted up upon the cross that thereby He might draw all of us into His loving embrace. Your Saviour is your lift. He is your ever-rising air. There is no limit to how high you can climb with Him. Jesus Christ lives to lift.
sat-pm-7-kearon.why: Beautiful close, 26 s, depends on the metaphor being set up.

sat-pm-8-dunn.hook: Without fanfare or fuss, he simply shouldered my heaviest burden.
sat-pm-8-dunn.text: A week or so later, a photograph from the race arrived in the mail. Miraculously, a friend captured that exact moment when Ted and I parted ways. But it also revealed a startling secret. As I looked closer, I saw what Ted really did for me that day. Much to my astonishment, I saw that he wasn’t only carrying his water; he was carrying two of my water bottles and my pack—which he dutifully toted every step of those last 10 grueling miles. Somehow, there on the side of the trail, with me in deep despair and ready to quit, he quietly lightened my load—strapping my hydration pack to his own waist. Without fanfare or fuss, he simply shouldered my heaviest burden.
sat-pm-8-dunn.why: The reveal of the talk: the photo shows Ted carrying his water and pack; a perfect picture of the Savior; nearly exact.

sat-pm-8-dunn.hook: “I know you can do this, Mike, and I’m going to get you there.”
sat-pm-8-dunn.text: Collapsing in the shade of a tree, I looked over at Ted and quietly said, “I give up.” But even as my resignation settled in, I got what you could arguably call the world’s first-ever “Ted Talk”! In a gentle, reassuring tone, he reminded me of the months of preparation and those early-morning runs. He then kneeled down, looked me in the eye, and said something I will never forget: “I know you can do this, Mike, and I’m going to get you there.” Those simple, sincere words sparked something inside me. After a few more minutes, I got to my feet. At first I walked, then hobbled into, well, a pretty solid shuffle. And somehow, step by step, together we conquered those last 10 miles.
sat-pm-8-dunn.why: Mile 90, "I give up," the "Ted Talk," and getting back up; humour plus emotion.

sat-pm-8-dunn.hook: In other words, the Redeemer rescues not by shortening our course but by helping us lengthen our stride.
sat-pm-8-dunn.text: In other words, the Redeemer rescues not by shortening our course but by helping us lengthen our stride. Anytime we turn to Christ, we turn a corner. By His grace we can trust and expect His constant care. And because God knows our prayers even before we ask Him, it’s reasonable to assume that blessings may often materialize in the selfsame moment we verbalize. His grace, which is a duality defined as a “divine means of help or strength,” can free us from the freight we would otherwise carry. And even when we don’t perceive Him at our side, He enlists the Teds—both of this world and sometimes even the Teds beyond—with His heartening promise of angels all around us to bear us up.
sat-pm-8-dunn.why: Quotable doctrine of grace ("Anytime we turn to Christ, we turn a corner."); exact.

sat-pm-8-dunn.hook: Other times He simply sends us a Ted.
sat-pm-8-dunn.text: All these years later, when I glance at that photo and ponder the metaphorical “last 10 miles” I still often face in this sojourn called life, I’m reminded that sometimes the God who makes the impossible possible can part seas and move mountains. Other times He simply sends us a Ted. But most often He tops off our courage, capacity, and confidence by empowering us to “lay aside every weight” so we can “run with patience the race that is set before us.”
sat-pm-8-dunn.why: Nice close, but the first sentence timing is partly interpolated.

sat-pm-8-dunn.hook: He not only knows the road; He knows you and what you, as noble offspring of the divine, are capable of.
sat-pm-8-dunn.text: One of the main reasons I trusted Ted during the race is the same reason we can implicitly trust Jesus in every aspect of our lives. Because He “marked the path and led the way,” there is no portion of our mortal sojourn He has not trod. He not only knows the road; He knows you and what you, as noble offspring of the divine, are capable of.

sat-pm-9-eyring.hook: He told me a single thought came to his mind at that moment: “I can’t fix this.”
sat-pm-9-eyring.text: Recently a friend of mine received a call from his wife informing him that their young married son had unexpectedly passed away the night before. He told me a single thought came to his mind at that moment: “I can’t fix this.” We are trained from a young age to solve problems, to be independent, to have perseverance and resilience. But our apparent self-reliance masks a deeper reality: All of us, regardless of experience, talent, or willpower, will sooner or later encounter burdens we cannot possibly carry ourselves.
sat-pm-9-eyring.why: Arresting opening anyone can feel; universal truth about burdens we cannot carry alone.

sat-pm-9-eyring.hook: He knows exactly how we feel, especially in our darkest and most trying times.
sat-pm-9-eyring.text: It is important to not allow our challenges to negatively impact our faith. Our Savior, Jesus Christ, suffered for us. He knows exactly how we feel, especially in our darkest and most trying times. As you humbly turn to the Lord and cast your burdens on Him, you have His promise: “Draw near unto me and I will draw near unto you.” He will provide comfort; He will provide answers on His timetable as you turn to Him.
sat-pm-9-eyring.why: Clear, comforting promise in 34 s; exact.

sat-pm-9-eyring.hook: As he and his wife left that evening, their countenances shone with the light of the One in whom we must all put our complete trust.
sat-pm-9-eyring.text: While in the hospital following the loss of the young couple’s twin baby, the new mother received a priesthood blessing. The husband, however, did not. After our dinner together, I had the opportunity to give this grieving father a priesthood blessing. Through the whisperings of the Spirit, he was promised peace “which passeth all understanding” during this difficult time and throughout his life. As he and his wife left that evening, their countenances shone with the light of the One in whom we must all put our complete trust.
sat-pm-9-eyring.why: Tender ministering story with a hopeful ending; exact.

sat-pm-9-eyring.hook: Our mortal journey is designed to try our faith.
sat-pm-9-eyring.text: Our mortal journey is designed to try our faith. Our challenges will be different depending on personal circumstance and even where we live in the world. I know that some of you worry about having enough food each day for you and your family. All of us face eventual limitations of physical or emotional health or the health of loved ones. We mourn when those close to us stray from the gospel path. We can be hurt by someone we love or hurt by the pain we have caused someone we love. We may feel misunderstood or deeply lonely. We might have a bad habit we’ve tried to overcome repeatedly without success.
sat-pm-9-eyring.why: Relatable list of real struggles (food, health, loneliness, habits); exact.

sat-pm-9-eyring.hook: There is hope in Jesus Christ.
sat-pm-9-eyring.text: We have received repeated prophetic warnings that in coming days we will not survive spiritually without the constant influence of the Holy Ghost. One reason is that in a world of increasing temporal and spiritual turbulence, true sources of comfort will become more scarce. Without divine comfort, we risk losing hope; and without hope, we can lose our faith and stop trying. Our hearts can fail us. There is hope in Jesus Christ.
sat-pm-9-eyring.why: Sober and exact, 36 s, less narrative.

sat-pm-10-rasband.hook: We preach, cajole, argue, demand, lecture, ignore, sit them down to watch general conference, and even send them links to the talks, like this one, but to no avail.
sat-pm-10-rasband.text: In our grief, we continuously ponder the whys, hows, and what ifs. We feel we have failed. We spend sleepless nights going over how we tried to draw our loved ones close to Jesus Christ and the Spirit. We preach, cajole, argue, demand, lecture, ignore, sit them down to watch general conference, and even send them links to the talks, like this one, but to no avail. If anything, these efforts can cause a greater rift. By divine design, brothers and sisters, everyone must choose for themselves to follow Jesus Christ.
sat-pm-10-rasband.why: Disarmingly honest and funny about wayward loved ones, then the key principle (agency).

sat-pm-10-rasband.hook: We cannot change their hearts, but He can; He is a God of miracles.
sat-pm-10-rasband.text: Listen carefully. I ask you to turn over to Jesus Christ your despair for those wayward souls. We cannot change their hearts, but He can; He is a God of miracles. We love our family members and friends profoundly, but they are foremost children of our Father in Heaven, who knows and loves them even more than we do. Our Father, the great Elohim, gave His Beloved Son the authority and power necessary to heal all His children. That is the good news of the gospel. By the power of Jesus Christ’s Atonement, there is always a way back!
sat-pm-10-rasband.why: The talk's core counsel and hope ("there is always a way back!"); exact.

sat-pm-10-rasband.hook: What brought him back? It was love.
sat-pm-10-rasband.text: Remember the prodigal son who chose to leave his safe moorings for “riotous living.” He lost his fortune and his self-respect, and he returned home in a wretched state. “When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran [to him].” “He was lost” and now was “found.” What brought him back? It was love. He knew where to find it. Love, brothers and sisters, is the answer to connecting with all of our loved ones.
sat-pm-10-rasband.why: Familiar parable distilled to "It was love."; exact.

sat-pm-10-rasband.hook: Never let a problem to be solved become more important than a person to be loved.
sat-pm-10-rasband.text: I close with three suggestions to help us find rest: First, let go of any guilt. We fail only when we give up and stop trying, so never, never give up on those you love. Remember the example of Alma praying for his son. Second, follow the admonition of President Thomas S. Monson: “Never let a problem to be solved become more important than a person to be loved.” Third, remember Jesus Christ is the answer. He is, always has been, and always will be. Seek Him through study of the scriptures and words of prophets, apostles, men and women leaders who are devoted to serving the Lord. And pray. Pray mightily to our Heavenly Father in the name of Jesus Christ. He will not leave us “comfortless.”
sat-pm-10-rasband.why: Practical three-step close incl. a classic Monson quote; exact; 66 s.

sat-pm-10-rasband.hook: Love is being there with arms outstretched and a cheerful countenance.
sat-pm-10-rasband.text: Love is not stepping back or sanctioning others’ decisions and actions. Love is being interested in their lives, their successes, and their challenges. Love is being there with arms outstretched and a cheerful countenance. Love is lifting with faith and hope in our Lord and Savior. Love relies upon the calming influence of the Holy Ghost.
sat-pm-10-rasband.why: Exact, lyrical list, 27 s; less narrative.

sat-pm-10-rasband.text: I promise you, as an Apostle of the Lord Jesus Christ, that when the devil sends “forth his mighty winds” pulling loved ones off course, “his mighty storm … shall have no power … to drag you down to the gulf of misery and endless wo, because of the rock upon which ye are built.” If that rock is Jesus Christ. Trust Him. He’s got this!
sat-pm-10-rasband.why: Great ending line, but "wo" timing differs and the scripture is dense.

sun-am-1-eyring.hook: She smiled and said firmly, “Hal, of course it’s hard. It’s supposed to be. Life is a test.”
sun-am-1-eyring.text: It is important to realize that the promise is not for the removal of challenges. My wise mother taught me that when I was a little boy. I had asked her, “Mother, why is life so hard?” She smiled and said firmly, “Hal, of course it’s hard. It’s supposed to be. Life is a test.” Years later I realized that as she spoke those words to me, she was passing through tests of her own and rising up through a lifetime of terrible medical trials. As a girl, she had been diagnosed with diseases that would cause lifelong health challenges. But because she knew the words “Fear not, I am with thee” were true, the Lord’s promise was fulfilled for her.
