sun-am-1-eyring.why: A mother's simple wisdom ("Life is a test") from a prophet's childhood, revealed as hard-won faith; name "Hal" interpolated.

sun-am-1-eyring.hook: You might reasonably wonder why a loving and all-powerful God allows our mortal test to be so hard.
sun-am-1-eyring.text: You might reasonably wonder why a loving and all-powerful God allows our mortal test to be so hard. It is because He knows that we must grow in spiritual cleanliness and stature to be able to live in His presence. To make that possible, Heavenly Father gave us a Savior and the power to choose for ourselves by faith to keep His commandments and to repent and to come unto Him. The Savior not only understands and has felt grief, but He has “borne [your] griefs, and carried [your] sorrows.” He knows you perfectly. He knows your heart.
sun-am-1-eyring.why: Answers the hardest question in under a minute and ends on "He knows your heart."; exact.

sun-am-1-eyring.hook: After she died, my father walked through the floor of the hospital ward to thank and to shake the hand of every nurse who had helped her.
sun-am-1-eyring.text: As my mother went through her last days of life, she became bedridden. The only picture she had placed on her bedroom wall was of the Savior. It hung where she could see it as she lay in her bed. My father had a cot placed next to her in the hospital room so that he could help her immediately during the nights. After she died, my father walked through the floor of the hospital ward to thank and to shake the hand of every nurse who had helped her. Now, I tell that story to offer evidence that the Lord sends faithful disciples to help Him keep His promise to succor others in their distress.
sun-am-1-eyring.why: Quiet, moving family memory turned into how the Lord succors through others.

sun-am-1-eyring.hook: Even your simple attention was a comfort.
sun-am-1-eyring.text: You have prayed in faith consistently for your family members or friends to know who the Lord would have you help for Him. As a face or a name has come into your mind, you have reached out to them. Even your simple attention was a comfort. That you felt prompted to reach out to them was evidence to them that the Lord knew and loved them.
sun-am-1-eyring.why: Gratitude to everyday ministers; short and exact.

sun-am-1-eyring.hook: Your kindness to them, even for a few seconds, or simply a warm smile can be a strengthening of their faith that the Lord is watching over them.
sun-am-1-eyring.text: Many of you have recognized a discouraged missionary as an invitation to lift a servant of Jesus Christ. Wherever they serve, missionaries are being stretched and they are praying for strength. Whatever they are assigned to do, they are in need of encouragement. Your kindness to them, even for a few seconds, or simply a warm smile can be a strengthening of their faith that the Lord is watching over them. When you speak to them, you will find words to build their faith that the Lord knows them and is aware of their circumstances.

sun-am-2-chibota.hook: It communicates, “I recognize you. I respect you. You matter.”
sun-am-2-chibota.text: As a child, I learned that greetings in my culture communicate love, concern, respect, and belonging. My daughter recently reminded me of the significance of the southern African greeting sawubona, which means, “I see you.” This greeting is much more than a simple “hello.” It is an acknowledgment of another person’s worth and humanity. It communicates, “I recognize you. I respect you. You matter.” The Savior Jesus Christ perfectly exemplified this principle. Throughout His ministry, He truly saw the people around Him. He saw the woman at the well, the leper, the blind man, and the child. Where others saw labels, He saw beloved sons and daughters of God.
sun-am-2-chibota.why: Beautiful cultural hook (sawubona = "I see you") tied straight to how Jesus saw people.

sun-am-2-chibota.hook: He told us, “Very few students know my name. Your daughter sees me.”
sun-am-2-chibota.text: Often, helping others feel seen as children of God begins with something as simple as learning their name. During our daughter’s final parent-teacher conference, a school janitor approached my husband and me. With tears in his eyes, he thanked us for our daughter. He explained that she regularly greeted him, knew his name, and even helped him clean up after lunch. He told us, “Very few students know my name. Your daughter sees me.”
sun-am-2-chibota.why: Tiny, true story with a lump-in-the-throat ending; exact.

sun-am-2-chibota.hook: Whatever labels may weigh heavily upon you today, Jesus Christ can raise you above them.
sun-am-2-chibota.text: Whatever labels may weigh heavily upon you today, Jesus Christ can raise you above them. His grace is sufficient to lift you above every label and limitation. Before we were students, athletes, employees, parents, citizens, or leaders, we were spirit children of our Heavenly Father. That eternal identity does not change when circumstances change, when we make mistakes, or when others misunderstand us. He loves you. He knows you. He sees you as you are now and sees who you will become. He has a plan for your life, and Jesus Christ is at the center of that plan!
sun-am-2-chibota.why: Direct identity message ("He loves you. He knows you."); one word timing differs.

sun-am-2-chibota.text: My dear friends, I leave you a final sawubona. I see you. More important, your Heavenly Father sees you. Your Savior, Jesus Christ, sees you. They know your name, your circumstances, your gifts, and your divine potential. As we learn to see ourselves and one another as They do, our homes, wards, schools, and communities will become places of belonging, healing, and love.
sun-am-2-chibota.why: Warm closing benediction; small timing differences on "sawubona".

sun-am-2-chibota.hook: Learn the name of someone who may feel unseen.
sun-am-2-chibota.text: I learned that when we ask Heavenly Father to help us see others, He guides us to those who feel unseen. You too can make a difference in someone’s life today simply by seeing them and acknowledging them. Remember that every person has divine worth. When we see one another through the Savior’s eyes, hearts change, relationships deepen, and faith grows. This week, I invite you to: Learn the name of someone who may feel unseen. Pray to see others as Heavenly Father sees them. Replace worldly labels with these eternal truths: Child of God. Child of the covenant. Disciple of Jesus Christ.

sun-am-3-andersen.hook: We need stillness to nourish our faith in Christ.
sun-am-3-andersen.text: Our world is in constant commotion. Our phone seems almost attached to our hand, bringing a flood of information, misinformation, and now artificial information. I grew up on a small dairy farm. For a season our three dozen cows were housed near a small canyon. Nearly every summer morning after milking, I would saddle my horse and guide the cows into a high meadow to graze, with no cell phone, no earbuds, no music, no texting. All day long, just me and the cows, alone with my thoughts. Times have changed, but our spirits have not changed. We need stillness to nourish our faith in Christ.
sun-am-3-andersen.why: Phone vs. a boy alone with dairy cows: vivid, relatable, exact.

sun-am-3-andersen.hook: “Our family is safe,” Cody and Haylee Woodbury said to me, “and our faith is secure.
sun-am-3-andersen.text: A month ago I accompanied President Dieter F. Uchtdorf to Spokane, Washington, where fires destroyed more than 800 homes. We visited members whose neighborhoods were completely destroyed. “Our family is safe,” Cody and Haylee Woodbury said to me, “and our faith is secure. We can build another house.” Their faith in Jesus Christ lifted their courage, and their courage has elevated their faith.
sun-am-3-andersen.why: Real, recent example of faith after losing a home to fire; 33 s.

sun-am-3-andersen.hook: But with courage born of her faith, she powerfully declared that in happiness or unspeakable grief, she would trust in the rock of her salvation, her Savior, Jesus Christ.
sun-am-3-andersen.text: Recently a noble woman of deep faith shared her testimony in church. Confidentially, I knew that she had been devastated by the betrayal of her husband. But with courage born of her faith, she powerfully declared that in happiness or unspeakable grief, she would trust in the rock of her salvation, her Savior, Jesus Christ. With our hope alive in Christ, even with life’s challenges, we too may be, as the Apostle Paul said, “troubled on every side, yet not distressed; … perplexed, but not in despair.”
sun-am-3-andersen.why: Moving example of courage after betrayal; ends with Paul's "not in despair".

sun-am-3-andersen.hook: President Oaks reflected, “Gathering all my faith, I accepted the call.”
sun-am-3-andersen.text: It is our faith in Jesus Christ that gives us the courage to accept a calling from our priesthood leaders even when we feel inadequate or without sufficient time to accept the responsibility. As a young attorney, President Dallin H. Oaks was energetically working in a prestigious law firm, including working evenings and Saturdays. His stake president called him to be a counselor in the stake mission presidency, necessitating at least three to four evenings per week. President Oaks reflected, “Gathering all my faith, I accepted the call.” President Oaks described this as a very important decision in his life. His faith strengthened his courage, and his decision brought increasing faith.
sun-am-3-andersen.why: A young President Oaks choosing faith over career; exact.

sun-am-3-andersen.hook: Her story is an example of courage born of faith in Jesus Christ.
sun-am-3-andersen.text: We welcome President Rosemary Chibota to the general leadership of the Church. Her story is an example of courage born of faith in Jesus Christ. Seventeen-year-old Rosemary found a Joseph Smith pamphlet missionaries had left at her home in Zimbabwe. She read it and immediately received a spiritual witness that it was true; Joseph had seen God the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ. She was taught and baptized and became an example to her parents, who joined the Church 19 years later. Faith and courage are hallmarks of disciples of Jesus Christ.
sun-am-3-andersen.why: Nice link to the previous speaker; name timing interpolated.

sun-am-4-fantone.hook: Time did not change—the missionaries did.
sun-am-4-fantone.text: As a mission president, I held regular interviews. In their first few months, it was not uncommon for some to sit across from me in tears and say, “President, I am so sad, lonely, and homesick. The days feel so long and time is so slow; I don’t even know if I can last for three more months.” Yet these valiant missionaries got on their knees, put on their name tags, and went out to serve anyway. A year later those exact same missionaries would sit in my office with glowing faces and say, “President, I am so happy! I love the people, and I love this work. But time is moving too fast—I don’t want this to end!” Every time I witnessed this transformation, I marveled. “Did time actually change?” You and I know the answer. Time did not change—the missionaries did. The work did not change—the workers did. Our missionaries changed.
sun-am-4-fantone.why: Before-and-after missionary interviews with a crisp payoff; 70 s.

sun-am-4-fantone.hook: The question: What’s in a name?
sun-am-4-fantone.text: Upon arriving, I handed the paperwork to the registrar. She passed a document back, pointed to a line at the bottom, and asked me to write my daughter’s name and sign above it. However, my mind was preoccupied. I mistakenly thought she had instructed me to write my name. With full confidence, I wrote “James Fantone” and signed. A few seconds later, I realized my error. “Well,” I thought, “no big deal. This is an easy fix.” You see, our youngest daughter’s name is Amanda James Fantone. So I simply added “Amanda” right before my own name, and the error was quickly fixed. Later, in a quiet moment of reflection, a profound question and a familiar scripture came to my mind. The question: What’s in a name?
sun-am-4-fantone.why: Funny, self-deprecating signature mix-up that opens into a gospel question; exact.

sun-am-4-fantone.hook: if by chance they knocked on our door, and if the boys’ and girls’ rooms were occupied, my parents would have gladly offered their room.
sun-am-4-fantone.text: I distinctly remember a season when the boys’ room was not available for us to use. My mother, a public school teacher, learned that one of her recently graduated students could not pursue his vocational studies because his family could not afford housing near the school. Desiring to help him fulfill his potential, my parents opened our home and offered him the boys’ room. During another season, it was the girls’ room that was occupied by someone else. When the Relief Society president in the ward spoke of a vulnerable family whose children desperately needed a safe place to stay, my parents, without hesitation, opened our doors, and some of the children indefinitely moved into our sisters’ room. I believe with all my heart that if my parents had lived in Bethlehem when Joseph was searching for a place for Mary to give birth, and if by chance they knocked on our door, and if the boys’ and girls’ rooms were occupied, my parents would have gladly offered their room.
sun-am-4-fantone.why: Parents who kept giving their children's rooms away; a son's tribute; 75 s.

sun-am-4-fantone.hook: My beloved brothers and sisters, the Savior’s invitation is not for us to merely add His name to our names.
sun-am-4-fantone.text: My beloved brothers and sisters, the Savior’s invitation is not for us to merely add His name to our names. His invitation is for us to take upon us His name by covenant and to serve Him with all our heart, might, mind, and strength—by lifting, loving, and serving our fellow men. I stand before you today as a witness of His living reality. I have made a sacred covenant to take upon myself the name of Jesus Christ, and I am determined to strive to serve Him faithfully to the end. I testify that He lives, that this is His restored Church, and that as we lose our lives in His service, we will find Him and we will find ourselves.
sun-am-4-fantone.why: Strong summary and testimony, exact, 50 s; less story.

sun-am-5-dube.hook: We do not need to perfect ourselves to come to Christ. We come to Christ to be perfected.
sun-am-5-dube.text: Three key truths to note: Come: It’s an action. We choose to move from our current place to a better place. Deny yourselves: Surrender. Let go of the things that are holding us back. Be perfected in Him: Come as we are with a willing heart. He will give us a new heart. We do not need to perfect ourselves to come to Christ. We come to Christ to be perfected.
sun-am-5-dube.why: Memorable reversal that frees people who feel unworthy; exact.

sun-am-5-dube.hook: At the mission office, a sign on the gate read, “Trespassers will be prosecuted.”
sun-am-5-dube.text: In 1987, I was a young missionary with only two years in the Church. At the mission office, a sign on the gate read, “Trespassers will be prosecuted.” President Oaks asked that it be removed to avoid any impression of exclusion. Rather, we invite all to come unto Christ through faith in Him and His Atonement. In that moment, I gained the desire to love others as the Savior does.
sun-am-5-dube.why: Concrete image: President Oaks asked that a Trespassers sign be removed, to invite all to Christ; exact.

sun-am-5-dube.hook: In the early hours of the morning, the answer came very clear: ‘Randall doesn’t need to be perfect.
sun-am-5-dube.text: Sister Child shared this with me later: “I stayed awake all night because I couldn’t bear watching Randall suffer—wanting to be perfect in every way possible. So all night I cried and pleaded with the Lord to help him. In the early hours of the morning, the answer came very clear: ‘Randall doesn’t need to be perfect. He needs to do the very best he can.’” Randall added: “I had trust in the Lord. But when I heard Laurin praying for me—saying all I needed to do was the best I could—I knew then that she was an answer to my prayers.”
sun-am-5-dube.why: Tender answer to a wife's all-night prayer; a few name timings interpolated.

sun-am-5-dube.hook: The adversary wants to hang that sign on the gate of our heart.
sun-am-5-dube.text: And that is why President Oaks had the sign on the gate taken down: “Trespassers will be prosecuted.” The adversary wants to hang that sign on the gate of our heart. Addiction, doubt, pride, pain, grief, guilt, materialism—or whatever is holding us back—he tells us this makes us unworthy to come unto Christ. But Moroni taught it. Laurin heard it. Randall lived it. You too can live it. If you will “deny not his power, then are ye sanctified in Christ by the grace of God, through the shedding of the blood of Christ.”
sun-am-5-dube.why: Great callback, but several small timing differences.

sun-am-6-cook.hook: He compared repentance to the feelings he had when he arrived back in England, departed from the battleship, and felt the earth of his island home under his feet.
sun-am-6-cook.text: When I was a young missionary in the British Mission, one of my most memorable experiences was teaching a wonderful man who had served on a battleship in the European theater during World War II, 16 years before we met him. When we taught him the principles of repentance, he was overcome with emotion. He then shared with us the feelings he was experiencing while being taught, especially about repentance. He compared repentance to the feelings he had when he arrived back in England, departed from the battleship, and felt the earth of his island home under his feet. It had overwhelmed him, and he fell to his knees in appreciation.
sun-am-6-cook.why: Unforgettable image of repentance from a WWII sailor; exact.

sun-am-6-cook.hook: Any use of the internet to bully, destroy a reputation, or place a person in a bad light is reprehensible.
sun-am-6-cook.text: Any use of the internet to bully, destroy a reputation, or place a person in a bad light is reprehensible. It is clear that evil communications are not just a matter of bad manners. If practiced by Latter-day Saints, they can adversely affect others who do not have a knowledge of God or a testimony of our Savior. The Lord has inspired marvelous technology that provides us with unparalleled experiences and opportunities when used wisely. The Church has experienced physical and verbal attacks over the years. We cannot control the conduct of others, but we can strive to be a peaceable people who live in accordance with the Christlike conduct and virtues taught by our Savior, Jesus Christ.
sun-am-6-cook.why: Timely, direct counsel on online conduct; one word differs.

sun-am-6-cook.hook: This message, “Whate’er thou art, act well thy part,” was so important and had such an impact on Elder McKay that he used it for inspiration as a missionary and for the rest of his life.
sun-am-6-cook.text: Mary and I recently had the privilege of meeting with the missionaries in the Scotland/Ireland Mission. On the grounds of one building there is a replica of a message that significantly influenced President David O. McKay when he was a young missionary in Scotland. As a new missionary, Elder McKay passed a building where the stone above the doorway bore this carved inscription: “WHAT-E’ER THOU ART ACT WELL THY PART.” This message, “Whate’er thou art, act well thy part,” was so important and had such an impact on Elder McKay that he used it for inspiration as a missionary and for the rest of his life. He determined that whatever responsibility he had, he would do his very best.
sun-am-6-cook.why: Classic McKay story with a motto viewers can keep; archaic spelling "Whate’er" timing interpolated.

sun-am-6-cook.hook: The ultimate reward of integrity and virtue is the constant companionship of the Holy Ghost.
sun-am-6-cook.text: We show our integrity by living virtuous lives and caring for and serving others. The ultimate reward of integrity and virtue is the constant companionship of the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost does not attend us when we do evil. But when we do what is right, He can dwell with us and guide us in all that we do. Part of having integrity is acknowledging our faults to the Lord and repenting of transgressions. When we make repentance a constant, day-to-day part of our lives, we can approach the Lord with integrity and receive His saving blessings.

sun-am-7-kyungu.hook: Rather than choosing words and language that escalate feelings of anger, disappointment, and frustration, let us use words that encourage understanding and peace.
sun-am-7-kyungu.text: Rather than choosing words and language that escalate feelings of anger, disappointment, and frustration, let us use words that encourage understanding and peace. We must choose language that strengthens confidence and preserves relationships. Words such as: “Please.” “Thank you.” “I appreciate that.” “I respect your view.” “This is a good point.” “Let us slow down and talk.” “We can work this out.” “It is OK.” “Let us stay calm.” “We don’t have to rush.” “I care about you.” “I am here for you.” “You are not alone.” “How are you feeling?” “That matters to me.” “I’m sorry.” “Please forgive me.” “I forgive you.” “Let us start again.” “I don’t want this to divide us.”
sun-am-7-kyungu.why: A practical list of peacemaking phrases anyone can use today ("Let us start again."); nearly exact.

sun-am-7-kyungu.text: I believe that all of us in this mortal journey have been hurt by some form of humiliating, degrading, or discouraging language from a family member, a colleague at work, a friend, or even a fellow member of the Church. There are expressions and words that can damage relationships and therefore need to be forgone in our communication. Examples include: “You are useless.” “You are stupid.” “You never do anything right.” “What is wrong with you?” “This is all your fault.” “You always mess things up.” “You never listen.” “You caused this problem.” “Leave me alone.” “I do not care.” “I do not need you in my life.” “I do not care about you.” “Just stop talking.” “I am tired of you.” The list could go on. Such words never edify. They weaken love, diminish respect, and damage relationships.
sun-am-7-kyungu.why: Recognisable list of hurtful phrases; powerful contrast clip. Some "I do not" spoken as contractions.

sun-am-7-kyungu.hook: It is not a simple suggestion; it is a call to discipleship as we follow Jesus Christ.
sun-am-7-kyungu.text: This invitation to forgo contention by using the language of peacemakers comes from the living prophet. It is not a simple suggestion; it is a call to discipleship as we follow Jesus Christ. I began pondering on President Oaks’s invitation and how I could act with faith accordingly. It is a spiritual exercise to identify the language and expressions we need to forgo and then replace them with words and phrases that bring peace wherever we are and at all times.
sun-am-7-kyungu.why: Frames the prophet's invitation as discipleship; one name timing interpolated.

sun-am-7-kyungu.hook: Let us pray for peaceful communication among us, regardless of the difference in our opinions.
sun-am-7-kyungu.text: Therefore, let us fill our hearts with the true doctrine of Christ, which has the power to change our language and help us speak more as peacemakers today, tomorrow, and always. As we follow Jesus Christ, we will not only feel His peace, but, as Elder Ulisses Soares said, “We can become instruments of His peace in the world.” Let us repent for the harsh language and expressions that have offended our friends, leaders, family members, or colleagues. Let us pray for peaceful communication among us, regardless of the difference in our opinions. Let us use the language that uplifts, edifies, comforts, and brings people together. Let us speak with “warm respect when we speak with each other.” “Let us qualify for His blessings by using the language … of peacemakers.”

sun-am-8-schmeil.hook: In the sacrament prayer we have a good reminder that we do not need to be perfect to partake of the sacrament.
sun-am-8-schmeil.text: In the sacrament prayer we have a good reminder that we do not need to be perfect to partake of the sacrament. We need to be willing to take upon us His name, remember Him, and keep His commandments, and in return we have the promise to always have His Spirit with us. The sacrament is essential to have the Spirit and the strength to continue on the covenant path.

sun-am-8-schmeil.hook: To be receptive to the will of God, we must have faith in Christ, which means that we trust Him even when we don’t have all the answers.
sun-am-8-schmeil.text: According to this scripture, we need to be humble and have faith in Christ for the weak things to become strong. A central feature of humility is having a broken heart, which means to be receptive to the will of God. To be receptive to the will of God, we must have faith in Christ, which means that we trust Him even when we don’t have all the answers.
sun-am-8-schmeil.why: Clear definition of faith as trust; exact; 27 s.

sun-am-8-schmeil.hook: Covenants bind us to Jesus Christ because He is central to every covenant we make.
sun-am-8-schmeil.text: We show our faith in Christ by making and keeping covenants with God. “A covenant is a sacred promise between God and His children. God gives the conditions for the covenant, and His children agree to obey those conditions. God promises to bless His children as they fulfill the covenant.” Covenants bind us to Jesus Christ because He is central to every covenant we make.
sun-am-8-schmeil.why: Simple definition of a covenant; exact; 30 s.

sun-am-8-schmeil.hook: May we also consider our ways.
sun-am-8-schmeil.text: May we also consider our ways. Heavenly Father is not asking us to physically build the temple, but He is asking us to build a strong relationship with Him and His Son, Jesus Christ, through our covenants. He will magnify our efforts as we consider our ways and make the proper adjustments to make and keep covenants with Him. God knows what is best for us and is eager to bless us.
sun-am-8-schmeil.why: Title theme, but a few words timing-interpolated.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: Whatever they are, the way to overcome them is to get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: We all have present or future concerns or struggles we are trying to overcome. Those may include questions or doubts. Whatever they are, the way to overcome them is to get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ. Again and again, He has taught us that He is the way. Focus on developing your faith in God and the mission of His Son, Jesus Christ. Strong faith requires more than strong desire. It means daily trying, one step at a time, with prayer and scriptural learning.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: The talk's core counsel, universal ("we all"), complete arc from struggle to daily faith.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: We need to be patient with one another and, occasionally, even with ourselves.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: We need to be patient with one another and, occasionally, even with ourselves. Overcoming uncertainty and doubt—which may include resolving conflicts between the evolving understanding of science and the sometimes incomplete teachings of religion—can be a lengthy process. It involves building faith and strengthening humility. Hold on to the first article of faith even if something else is uncertain. And while you wait, wait upon the Lord, which includes trusting in His timing as well as in His promises.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Warm, relatable hook; speaks directly to people with doubts; ends on a clear promise.

sun-am-9-oaks.text: His grace is for all. Similarly, the Book of Mormon tells us that the children of God in “every nation” have His promise that He “manifesteth himself unto all those who believe in him, by the power of the Holy Ghost.” These promises from the Book of Mormon are true. Millions believe them and have had experiences to affirm their truth. I invite all to believe them.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Four-word hook that is the talk's title theme; ends on a prophetic invitation.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: We are all a work in progress.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: We are all a work in progress. We are all at different places on what President Russell M. Nelson called “the covenant path.” We need to be patient with one another and, occasionally, even with ourselves. Overcoming uncertainty and doubt—which may include resolving conflicts between the evolving understanding of science and the sometimes incomplete teachings of religion—can be a lengthy process. It involves building faith and strengthening humility. Hold on to the first article of faith even if something else is uncertain. And while you wait, wait upon the Lord, which includes trusting in His timing as well as in His promises.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Great hook, but printed "President Russell M. Nelson" is spoken "President Nelson", so captions would show 2 unspoken words; 65 s.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: A major source of concern to your prophet leaders are those members of diminishing faith in Jesus Christ. We love you, young and old, men and women. So does the Lord God! He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you. Because of this concern and according to His words, I urge you to keep the commandments and be true to the covenants so many of you have made to guide you along the covenant path. Never let your secular learning limit your spiritual horizons.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Moving line, but spoken wording differs from print in 3 places ("source of" not spoken; "young and old, men and women" order; "covenant/s").

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: These simple practices will protect and strengthen you.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: Protect yourself with the weekly renewing of your covenants by partaking of the sacrament and with consistent efforts to live according to those sacred covenants. Those who have been endowed should include regular attendance at the temple. These simple practices will protect and strengthen you.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Practical and short, but "renewing" is spoken "renewal"; less emotional.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: There is no ultimate conflict between knowledge obtained by these different methods because God, our omnipotent Eternal Father, knows all truth and expects us to learn by both methods.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: We are grateful to know that there are two methods of gaining needed knowledge: (1) the evolving disclosures of man through the scientific method and digital information, which may be inaccurate, and (2) the truths discovered through the spiritual method, which begins with faith in God and relies on scriptures, inspired teaching, and personal revelation. There is no ultimate conflict between knowledge obtained by these different methods because God, our omnipotent Eternal Father, knows all truth and expects us to learn by both methods.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Distinctive science-and-faith idea, but dense; printed "(1)/(2)" and "Eternal" differ from speech.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: As your President, I pray for what our Heavenly Father wants for each of us—to be active members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, proceeding forward on the covenant path into the eternities.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: As your President, I pray for what our Heavenly Father wants for each of us—to be active members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, proceeding forward on the covenant path into the eternities. We need one another’s prayers. I feel the positive effect of your prayers. I am thankful, and I love you.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Tender ("I love you"), but only ~35 s and "of Latter-day Saints" is not spoken.

sun-am-9-oaks.hook: All around us we see evidence that many in the world are hungry for our Savior, Jesus Christ, and His teachings.
sun-am-9-oaks.text: All around us we see evidence that many in the world are hungry for our Savior, Jesus Christ, and His teachings. As declared on its title page, the Book of Mormon has come forth that we “may know [of] the covenants of the Lord” and also for the convincing of all “that Jesus is the Christ, the Eternal God, manifesting himself unto all nations.” I call upon all to act on these truths and to share them with others that we may all draw closer to Jesus Christ, our Savior. I make this invitation and add my testimony of Him and His mission in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
sun-am-9-oaks.why: Strong close + testimony, but spoken "quote/end of quote" asides are not in the print (uncaptioned audio).

sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.hook: Have you ever noticed that the sacrament is the only ordinance we receive during which we are not addressed by name?
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.text: Have you ever noticed that the sacrament is the only ordinance we receive during which we are not addressed by name? Rather, it is performed for “the souls of all those who partake of it.” The only names that are used are those of God the Father and Jesus Christ. We partake individually but also as a group. There is something powerful, something empowering, about renewing covenants with God while surrounded by brothers and sisters who have made or are considering making the same covenants. The sacrament is a weekly reminder, a sacred reminder, that we are not alone. We have the Savior, and we have each other.
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.why: Fresh insight most members never noticed; ends "We have the Savior, and we have each other."; exact.

sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.hook: If we are not one, we are not His.
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.text: The catalyst for this change was Jesus Christ and His doctrine. It always has been, and it always will be. Jesus Christ has the power to change us—you and me—purify us, and unite us. The closer we come to Him, the closer we will come to each other—and the closer we will come to the unity He wants for us. If we are not one, we are not His.

sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.hook: Others unite around hobbies, professional interests, or even love for a favorite soccer team or brand of soft drink.
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.text: Throughout history, people have united over a variety of purposes. Some have united over social causes or political ideas. Some unite to celebrate their cultural heritage. Some, sadly, have united because of hatred for another group. Others unite around hobbies, professional interests, or even love for a favorite soccer team or brand of soft drink. Often these desires to unify are driven by very strong feelings or opinions. In the Savior’s Church, it is not our political views, culture, or personal interests that unite us. It is our love for God and neighbor, God’s children. It is our commitment to our covenants with Jesus Christ and to His restored gospel. We are “one in Christ.”
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.why: Light humour leading to what truly unites us; one word differs.

sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.hook: “The pool is getting deeper and deeper, and I can’t swim!”
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.text: My heart fills with gratitude when I think back on my own baptism. I was baptized at age eight in an impressive indoor public swimming pool. Back then, as we walked into the water, my mind and heart were preoccupied with this thought: “The pool is getting deeper and deeper, and I can’t swim!” Spiritual growth is rarely dramatic at the beginning. Like an exponential curve, it often starts gradually—with loving parents, simple prayers, and small acts of faith.
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.why: Charming childhood baptism memory; small timing differences.

sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.text: But the Savior of the world, the Son of God, transcended worldly boundaries and divisions. As Paul said, He “[broke] down the middle wall of partition between us.” He consistently reached out to those who would otherwise be shunned as outsiders. He touched lepers. He praised Gentiles for their faith. He used a Samaritan as an example of compassion. He gathered people from different walks of life and asked them to serve together in positions of trust. He ministered to the poor and rich alike. And today He continues to invite all to come unto Him.
sun-pm-1-uchtdorf.why: Good list of Christ uniting outsiders; one word differs.

sun-pm-2-spannaus.hook: Dear young women, the Lord knows where you are; He has your exact location and can guide you.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.text: I want to illustrate this concept with an experience. On my way to the dentist, I put the address in my phone. While I was driving on the freeway, the GPS thought I was on a parallel street and kept telling me to turn right—when there was no place to turn. Finally, I pulled off the freeway and called my husband for help. When I gave him my exact location, he was able to guide me to the place I wanted to go. Dear young women, the Lord knows where you are; He has your exact location and can guide you. He knows your dreams and your gifts. He knows when you feel alone and what your questions are. He knows your challenges and how to turn your weaknesses into strengths. He knows everything. And knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.why: Relatable GPS mishap to "He has your exact location"; ends "knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less."; exact.

sun-pm-2-spannaus.hook: “But the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are at your side.”
sun-pm-2-spannaus.text: Then my husband gave me a priesthood blessing, and in that moment, I felt the heavens open. In the blessing, I was told, “Satan wants to destroy your self-esteem, your mind, your thoughts, and your spirit.” And then I received these words: “But the Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are at your side.” Dear young women, I testify that the Lord has greater power than the enemy. He knows where you are and has promised to lead you by the hand. Always put Him first and remain faithful to the covenants you made at your baptism. Angels can minister to you. The Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are at your side.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.why: Personal low point answered in a blessing, then a testimony to every young woman; exact.

sun-pm-2-spannaus.hook: Dear young women, I testify that you are beloved daughters of heavenly parents, with a divine nature and an eternal destiny.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.text: Our Father and our Savior know you and have the same perfect love for you. Part of that love and mercy is giving us many opportunities and being patient as we learn and work on our list of aspirations. Dear young women, I testify that you are beloved daughters of heavenly parents, with a divine nature and an eternal destiny. Each of you has a crucial and important work to do here on earth. That work is different for each person, but if you choose to love God and Jesus Christ and to trust Them, doing that work will bring you the same great joy.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.why: Identity and purpose for youth; one word differs.

sun-pm-2-spannaus.hook: I felt depressed, as if I were in a black cloud.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.text: A few years ago, we had recently moved from Argentina to the United States, and I was learning English. (I am still learning!) At that time, my calling involved teaching. That day I felt everything I said had been wrong, that I had mispronounced words and made many grammatical errors—that it had been a complete disaster! I felt depressed, as if I were in a black cloud. I wondered why God had given me this calling if I couldn’t even speak! I was confused and didn’t see a way out. That night I went to sleep in tears, hoping I would feel better in the morning. But in the morning, I woke up feeling the same.
sun-pm-2-spannaus.why: Honest and relatable but sets up the blessing; printed aside "(I am still learning!)" differs slightly.

sun-pm-3-villanueva.hook: These blessings, both temporal and spiritual—and many others—are evidence that the Lord has indeed opened the windows of heaven and poured out His promised blessings in abundance.
sun-pm-3-villanueva.text: Elder Bednar’s words prompted me to make a list of the blessings I have received through faithfully paying my tithing. The Holy Ghost helped me recognize many blessings: I have enjoyed steady employment for many years. My wife, my children, and I have been blessed with good health. Our home and temporal possessions have been preserved, even during difficult times. The Lord has blessed me with the ability to manage my time and resources so I could obtain an education. I have developed the gift of gratitude by learning to appreciate the Lord’s hand in each of His tender mercies. I have learned to recognize the influence of the Holy Ghost when making important decisions in my life. These blessings, both temporal and spiritual—and many others—are evidence that the Lord has indeed opened the windows of heaven and poured out His promised blessings in abundance.
sun-pm-3-villanueva.why: Concrete list of quiet tithing blessings; invites viewers to make their own list.

sun-pm-3-villanueva.hook: Perhaps the change that required the greatest faith and sacrifice was to honorably pay a full tithe.
sun-pm-3-villanueva.text: When I was 10 years old, my family and I were baptized as members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Entering the covenant path brought some profound changes to our lives. I had never attended any church before. I now understand that those changes reflected our sincere efforts to apply the doctrine of Jesus Christ in our lives. Perhaps the change that required the greatest faith and sacrifice was to honorably pay a full tithe. Those were difficult years financially. My mother had separated from my father and worked tirelessly to provide for our family. Supporting eight children—most of us still very young—was no easy task.
sun-pm-3-villanueva.why: A single mother of eight choosing to pay tithing; two small differences.

sun-pm-3-villanueva.hook: Sometimes we expect the Lord’s blessings to come the way we would wish, rather than in His own way and timing.
sun-pm-3-villanueva.text: Sometimes we expect the Lord’s blessings to come the way we would wish, rather than in His own way and timing. After a sacrament meeting, a faithful sister shared that her testimony of the law of tithing had begun to weaken. She explained that although she had always paid a full tithe, she had never received the job promotion she had hoped for nor even the salary increase she deserved. The counsel I gave her is the same counsel I share with you today.
sun-pm-3-villanueva.why: Honest question from a sister who never got her raise; sets up the counsel; small differences.

sun-pm-4-bednar.hook: The answer to this question is an emphatic no!
sun-pm-4-bednar.text: In these cases, a faithful spouse may ask, “Can the unrighteous exercise of moral agency by another person rob me of what God has promised?” The answer to this question is an emphatic no! The unworthy actions of a spouse certainly bring heartache and sorrow to the other spouse and family members. However, unrighteousness by one person cannot hinder or thwart the flow of God’s love, strength, and blessings to another person. The power of the Lord’s infinite and eternal Atonement can overcome all things, all the time, everywhere, for every person who holds fast to their covenants with Him.
sun-pm-4-bednar.why: Deeply reassuring apostolic answer for anyone hurt by a spouse's choices.

sun-pm-4-bednar.hook: I do not know and cannot explain precisely how and when promised blessings are received. But I do know promised blessings will be received.
sun-pm-4-bednar.text: You may ask, “How can this be the case if a temple marriage does not endure?” The revealed doctrine of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints does not address all details of and nuances about such cases. I do not know and cannot explain precisely how and when promised blessings are received. But I do know promised blessings will be received. No faithful disciple will ultimately be deprived of any eternal blessing God has promised because of another individual’s unrighteous exercise of moral agency.
sun-pm-4-bednar.why: Humble, powerful "I do not know… But I do know"; exact.

sun-pm-4-bednar.hook: But the man had not taken good care of his passport.
sun-pm-4-bednar.text: Once a man wanted to visit family members in a distant country. He planned his trip, packed his suitcase, and traveled by airplane to the city where his relatives lived. The man excitedly exited the airplane and walked to the passport control checkpoint. He had a valid passport issued by an authorized agency of his country’s government. He presented his passport to a border official, who verified the man’s identity, nationality, and reasons for visiting the country. But the man had not taken good care of his passport. The personal information page had been stained and damaged. And a ripped page had been repaired in an unauthorized manner with tape and glue. Consequently, the border official rejected his passport and refused to provide the stamp necessary for him to enter the country. The man was disappointed and perplexed about what he should do next.
sun-pm-4-bednar.why: Clear modern parable; one phrase timing differs; 67 s.

sun-pm-4-bednar.hook: The lesson of this story is quite simple: the integrity of a passport must be maintained over time.
sun-pm-4-bednar.text: The lesson of this story is quite simple: the integrity of a passport must be maintained over time. Holding a valid passport provided the opportunity for the man to enter the country, but the passport alone did not guarantee he actually would be allowed to enter the country. Of course, this simple analogy has limitations. Unlike damage to a physical passport, the adversities and afflictions we experience through no fault of our own do not diminish God’s promises to us or invalidate our covenants.
sun-pm-4-bednar.why: Lesson of the parable plus the tender caveat about undeserved adversity; exact.

sun-pm-5-lebethoa.hook: Put together, our names mean “eternal joy.”
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.text: In my home country of South Africa, it is customary for parents to give their children names with special meaning. My name is Thabo. It means “joy.” My beloved wife’s middle name is Gadifele. It means “eternal or endless.” Put together, our names mean “eternal joy.” What an expectation! But shortly after we were married, a discussion one evening unexpectedly turned into our first serious disagreement. It quickly escalated into an argument, and we went from being a cheerful, happy couple to giving each other the silent treatment in a selfish state of quiet desperation.
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.why: Charming names story with an honest, funny turn ("What an expectation!"); name timings interpolated.

sun-pm-5-lebethoa.hook: The man was enlightened by the Spirit on the changes he needed to make and acted upon it.
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.text: Whilst we were serving as mission leaders in our home country, one of our missionaries shared a story of a man they were teaching who, after reading the Book of Mormon, took a shovel, dug a hole in his garden, emptied a newly purchased large tin of coffee into it, and buried it. The man was enlightened by the Spirit on the changes he needed to make and acted upon it. We too can receive enlightenment as we study our scriptures.
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.why: Memorable image (burying a new tin of coffee after reading the Book of Mormon).

sun-pm-5-lebethoa.hook: Through Him, today can be a new day and tomorrow can be a better day.
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.text: Whatever concerns, challenges, and struggles we may have in our lives, the answer is always Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ can bring light in our moments of darkness and restore hope where there is hopelessness. He knows where we have been, where we are, and where we need to be. Through Him, today can be a new day and tomorrow can be a better day.

sun-pm-5-lebethoa.hook: It is important to remember that we do not need to go through this alone.
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.text: Repentance means a change of mind and a turning of the heart to God. Let us ponder about the changes that we need to make in our lives, and these may include how we use our time, the things we watch or listen to, and the language and tone we use as we communicate with others. Perhaps we can begin by asking ourselves what is it that we need to change in our lives. It is important to remember that we do not need to go through this alone.
sun-pm-5-lebethoa.why: Gentle, practical invitation to repent; one phrase timing differs.

sun-pm-6-sinclair.hook: He did not hold her hostage to her history.
sun-pm-6-sinclair.text: He spoke to the woman with dignity, not shame. He earnestly listened to her questions and responded with teaching, not ridicule. He did not hold her hostage to her history. He trusted her with truth. Jesus Christ reminds us that to help people transform their lives, we must look not only to their past—we must look to their possible. She walked to the well that day as a pariah. She walked away from the well with a purpose. That is precisely what “quick to help and slow to judge” looks like.
sun-pm-6-sinclair.why: Rhythmic, quotable lines ("look not only to their past… to their possible"); exact.

sun-pm-6-sinclair.hook: James had unintentionally, but quite successfully, created a one-arm straitjacket.
sun-pm-6-sinclair.text: That Sabbath morning, my young friend James was wearing a new suit. As the program began, James was examining some of the more interesting aspects of his new suit. What most captured his attention were two features of his jacket. On his jacket sleeves there were buttons but no holes. And on the left lapel of his jacket there was a buttonhole but no buttons. Neither the buttons nor the buttonhole seemed to be serving any real purpose. Well, James cleverly devised a purpose for both. I anxiously watched as James delightedly buttoned his right sleeve to his left jacket lapel. Being pleased with himself quickly gave way to being panicked, because once James had buttoned his arm to his chest, even with the flexibility of a Primary child, he could not get himself loose. James had unintentionally, but quite successfully, created a one-arm straitjacket.

sun-pm-6-sinclair.hook: A little child led me to learn this: that a true disciple of Jesus Christ is quick to help and slow to judge.
sun-pm-6-sinclair.text: But instead of being aggravated, she wanted to help. Quickly discerning what action was needed, she reached up with her tiny, nonjudgmental fingers and popped the button out of the buttonhole. James was rescued, and the Primary program was saved! I felt relieved but also humbled. I recognized the quiet rebuke of a misplaced button and tiny fingers reminding me that I should be trying to be more like Jesus. That small but majestic moment helped me embrace what Elder Patrick Kearon has described as “a radical reorientation” of my soul. I don’t recall the topic of the Primary program that day, but the message I received through the Holy Ghost prompted a spiritual realignment. A little child led me to learn this: that a true disciple of Jesus Christ is quick to help and slow to judge.
sun-pm-6-sinclair.why: The rescue and the lesson (title line); a few names timing-interpolated.

sun-pm-6-sinclair.hook: To her, it was an ordinary day—until Jesus showed up.
sun-pm-6-sinclair.text: As the conversation opened, Jesus was weary and unexpectedly asked the woman for a drink. We can only imagine how many days this woman had been coming to this well at this hour, alone—until this day. To her, it was an ordinary day—until Jesus showed up. In her ordinary days, she may have endured many judging eyes but few helping hands—until this day.

sun-pm-7-stevenson.hook: As I swooped him up, he sang every word of the Primary song in his sweet, loud, young voice.
sun-pm-7-stevenson.text: Recently, I conducted a devotional with members in South America. Many were suffering because of a severe earthquake they had experienced. As I invited Primary children to stand and all to sing “I Am a Child of God,” out of the congregation, an incredibly young Primary boy got away from his parents and ran right up to the stand next to me. As I swooped him up, he sang every word of the Primary song in his sweet, loud, young voice. This testimony was so important and powerful, inviting the Spirit to comfort and testify to all that we are children of a loving Heavenly Father, even in the most difficult of times.
sun-pm-7-stevenson.why: Delightful true moment: a tiny boy runs to the stand and sings "I Am a Child of God" after an earthquake.

sun-pm-7-stevenson.hook: We witnessed a miraculous transformation: peace for despair, joy for sadness, hope for ashes.
sun-pm-7-stevenson.text: When I lived in Japan, I became friends with a Buddhist temple priest. He was a happy man. But when his wife died, leaving him alone, he became incredibly sad, even depressed. One night a friend and I visited him at his temple to minister to him. At first, he was reluctant to talk, so grief-stricken and inconsolable. When I asked him if he knew where his wife was, he at once lifted his head, startled at the question. “What do you mean?” We shared with him that the spirits of all men and women, when they pass away, “are taken home to that God who gave them life” and that in God’s loving plan for His children, the spirit of this man’s beloved wife, an honorable woman, was received into a place called the spirit world, where she could enter a state of rest, happiness, and peace. His countenance changed in that moment. It was as if we watched him partake of the fruit of the tree of life and his soul was filled “with exceedingly great joy.” We witnessed a miraculous transformation: peace for despair, joy for sadness, hope for ashes.
sun-pm-7-stevenson.why: Grieving Buddhist priest learns where his wife is; strong emotional arc; 85 s.

sun-pm-7-stevenson.hook: But once we have tasted it, we know how much we like it.
sun-pm-7-stevenson.text: Think for a moment about your favorite fruits. Are they pineapples, bananas, and grapes? Or mangoes, strawberries, and coconuts? We can hold the fruit, feel it, and look at it. We might smell it and guess how sweet it is. But once we have tasted it, we know how much we like it. Gospel truths are the same. We learn them at home, Primary, and through the scriptures. They become sweet to us as we live them, bringing us happiness and joy.
sun-pm-7-stevenson.why: Kid-friendly, playful analogy that adults love too.

sun-pm-7-stevenson.hook: I remember, when I was your age, my mother saying, many times, “Gary, pay attention and listen. Just one more talk.”
sun-pm-7-stevenson.text: When we speak in conference, we speak to everyone, but some of my message today will be more directly to you, children of Primary age. You know who you are—some watching from home and others in a Church building. As this is the last conference session, you may be tired or restless. I remember, when I was your age, my mother saying, many times, “Gary, pay attention and listen. Just one more talk.”
sun-pm-7-stevenson.why: Funny direct address to Primary kids; 30 s.

sun-pm-8-reid.hook: Each time I read the headline, I smile and think, “Thankfully, that headline didn’t share the names because I really hope people think I’m one of the scholars!”
sun-pm-8-reid.text: Shortly after I was sustained as a member of the Sunday School General Presidency, I felt inadequate, overwhelmed, and completely out of place. I realized later that I was not the only one trying to make sense of it because I saw a news headline that read, “New Sunday School Leaders Include Men Involved in Church Education and an NFL Player.” Each time I read the headline, I smile and think, “Thankfully, that headline didn’t share the names because I really hope people think I’m one of the scholars!” I especially feel that way today. Although the headline makes me laugh, it does not always quiet this feeling inside of me: “Lord, I love You, but do You really have the right person?” Perhaps you have asked yourself similar questions: Do I know enough? Am I good enough to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ?
sun-pm-8-reid.why: Self-deprecating humour (the NFL player) that opens into a question every teacher asks.

sun-pm-8-reid.hook: Brothers and sisters, if you are wondering whether you are good enough to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ, the answer is yes!
sun-pm-8-reid.text: Brothers and sisters, if you are wondering whether you are good enough to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ, the answer is yes! Not because you know everything. Not because you have every teaching skill. Not because you always feel capable or confident. Because you can love the Master Teacher! And as you deepen your love for the One you teach about, He will teach you, walk beside you, and gradually make you into the teacher He knows you can become. Whether you see yourself as a scholar, an athlete, a lifelong disciple, or someone who has recently started—or started again—to follow Christ, the invitation is the same. Come unto the Master Teacher. Learn of Him. Love Him. As you do, He will help you love those you teach—and that love will make your teaching more like His.
sun-pm-8-reid.why: Rousing, rhythmic answer ("Not because… Because you can love the Master Teacher!"); one word differs.

sun-pm-8-reid.hook: The impact of a gospel teacher is not just the message—it is the love of the messenger.
sun-pm-8-reid.text: Those truths were lovingly reinforced by faithful teachers in this little village chapel. Many of my earliest Primary classes were held beneath the shade of a mango tree. Our teachers faithfully prepared each lesson, but what I remember most is how they loved us. They knew us personally—even by name. Their love helped us feel the Savior’s love, and feeling His love helped us feel the truth of His gospel. Looking back, I realize my parents and my Church teachers were following the pattern of the Master Teacher. The impact of a gospel teacher is not just the message—it is the love of the messenger.
sun-pm-8-reid.why: Primary under a mango tree in Samoa; quotable payoff.

sun-pm-8-reid.hook: If class members leave the lesson feeling closer to the Savior than when they came, we have taught enough.
sun-pm-8-reid.text: Some may ask, “How can I teach everything in 25 minutes?” Perhaps the better question is “How can I help those I teach connect to the Savior sooner?” President Dallin H. Oaks taught, “A gospel teacher will never obscure [a learner’s] view of the Master by standing in the way.” The purpose of every lesson is not for people to leave talking about the teacher. It is for them to leave thinking about and loving the Savior. Twenty-five-minute lessons are not a limitation; they are an invitation: to focus, more clearly than ever, on helping others come to the Savior. If class members leave the lesson feeling closer to the Savior than when they came, we have taught enough.
sun-pm-8-reid.why: Timely for the new Sunday schedule; small differences.

sun-pm-9-gilbert.hook: I may have won the debate in the moment, but I lost the Spirit and I failed to help my struggling friend.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.text: I failed to see this with a friend who had at one time been spiritually faithful but was now attacking the Church. My frustration came not just because of his bitterness but because I knew he knew better. Unfortunately, rather than recognize the tension of the moment or that he might be hurting for reasons I could not see, I shot back an angry retort. I may have won the debate in the moment, but I lost the Spirit and I failed to help my struggling friend. That day I stood for truth, but I did it without love and without charity.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.why: Candid personal failure that teaches the whole talk; one word differs.

sun-pm-9-gilbert.hook: Resisting the impulse to initially respond built common ground, which allowed me later to teach from a place of love.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.text: A stake president once brought me a long list of ministering visits. I suggested he choose just one home, given our schedule limitations. Technically he honored the request. But when we arrived at the home, there were five separate individuals waiting inside, each with a completely different concern. I asked, “Well, where do you want to start?” As I listened to their stories, I was tempted at times to interject, but the Spirit kept prompting me to wait. After nearly two hours of listening, going right through our next meeting, I began to better understand their struggles and I could feel their heartfelt strivings. And when I invited them to come to stake conference that evening, each one of them accepted. Resisting the impulse to initially respond built common ground, which allowed me later to teach from a place of love.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.why: Funny set-up (five people in "one home") and a lesson in listening; 73 s.

sun-pm-9-gilbert.hook: Now, I know we follow the prophet, but I hesitantly, even sheepishly, replied that for the sake of the Church, maybe we should write out at least what I said.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.text: Several years ago I received an assignment to speak at Ensign College. President Oaks was the main devotional speaker, and he asked that I speak with him on some of the challenging doctrinal topics of the day. This was a daunting assignment. He then suggested that we not use formal written remarks. Now, I know we follow the prophet, but I hesitantly, even sheepishly, replied that for the sake of the Church, maybe we should write out at least what I said. He relented, and the devotional was entitled “Stand Fast with Love in Proclaiming Truth.” In the address, President Oaks shared five principles I have felt impressed to amplify today.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.why: Self-deprecating humour with President Oaks; one title timing differs.

sun-pm-9-gilbert.hook: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together.
sun-pm-9-gilbert.text: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together. I believe teaching truth with love will be the hallmark of Christ’s disciples in the last days. For some this will require greater conviction. For others it will demand greater charity. I know the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love.

sun-pm-10-oaks.hook: Truth is to be found here—truth about the teachings of the Lord and truth about the covenant path that will lead us to our destiny, the destiny desired by our Heavenly Father.
sun-pm-10-oaks.text: As we now go forward, we invoke the blessings of the Lord on you and your families, blessings of peace and contentment. And we bless your service of the Lord Jesus Christ in these challenging times. I close with my testimony. This is the restored gospel of Jesus Christ in His Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Truth is to be found here—truth about the teachings of the Lord and truth about the covenant path that will lead us to our destiny, the destiny desired by our Heavenly Father. Of all this I testify to you in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
sun-pm-10-oaks.why: Prophetic blessing and testimony that closes the conference; exact.

sun-pm-10-oaks.hook: On April 5, 2027, the temple doors will open to the public—the first such opening since 1893, 134 years ago.
sun-pm-10-oaks.text: As we look forward, we are welcoming the world, in person or virtually, to the Salt Lake Temple Celebration. On April 5, 2027, the temple doors will open to the public—the first such opening since 1893, 134 years ago. Join us at TempleSquare.org or through the Temple Square app to learn more. Following this session of general conference, the first episode of a dynamic video series, Dedicate, will premiere worldwide in multiple languages. More will come in the months ahead, including a virtual tour of the Salt Lake Temple.
sun-pm-10-oaks.why: Newsworthy Salt Lake Temple announcement people will share; one number timing interpolated; 67 s.

sun-pm-10-oaks.hook: As the talks of this conference are published, we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain.
sun-pm-10-oaks.text: My dear brothers and sisters, the great messages of this conference and the Spirit of the Lord have inspired all of us to concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies on the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ and His Father’s plan for our eternal increase and joy. As the talks of this conference are published, we invite all to study and ponder them prayerfully and to act in faith on the principles they explain. The Lord has promised, “Unto him that receiveth I will give more.”
sun-pm-10-oaks.why: The prophet's invitation to study conference; exact.
